https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE NATIONAL SCIENTIFIC CONVENTION ON HOMOEOPATHY AT BHUBANESWAR
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
President's Secretariat 
 PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE NATIONAL SCIENTIFIC CONVENTION ON HOMOEOPATHY AT BHUBANESWAR 
 OUR INSTITUTIONS, RESEARCHERS, TEACHERS AND HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS MUST CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS BUILDING AN ACCESSIBLE, EQUITABLE, SCIENTIFICALLY RESPONSIBLE AND RESPONSIVE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi 
 The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy at Bhubaneswar, Odisha today (November 25, 2026). 
 Speaking on the occasion, the President said that homoeopathy represents an important part of India's diverse healthcare landscape. Over the years, it has developed a wide institutional presence in India and has become accessible to people through educational institutions, healthcare facilities and public health networks. 
 The President underlined that the future credibility and academic standing of homoeopathy will depend significantly on the scientific integrity of its research and the quality of clinical evidence it generates. She urged research institutions, medical colleges, universities and professional organisations to collaborate in developing a strong research culture. She stated that the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy provides an excellent platform for meaningful academic engagement, institutional partnerships and a shared vision for the future. She advised participants, particularly young researchers and professionals, to make full use of this opportunity. 
 The President said that the development of homoeopathy should be accompanied by an unwavering commitment to scientific inquiry, academic excellence and professional accountability. Research should be guided by sound methodology, adequately designed clinical studies, systematic documentation and transparent reporting. She emphasised on the need to encourage multicentric studies, systematic reviews, evidence synthesis, pharmacological and fundamental research and the development of reliable clinical databases. She said that intellectual honesty to acknowledge research limitations, report unfavourable findings and allow scientific evidence to guide conclusions is equally important. 
 The President said that the medical profession demands much more than academic qualifications. It requires intellectual discipline, scientific temper, integrity, empathy and a commitment to lifelong learning. She urged the young practitioners of homoeopathy to cultivate the habit of questioning and never stop learning. She said that they should have the courage to investigate, the patience to seek evidence and the humility to accept new knowledge. They should never forget that behind every patient is a human being with hopes, fears and dignity. 
 The President said that as India advances towards the national goal of Viksit Bharat 2047, healthcare and education will remain two of its most important pillars. Our institutions, researchers, teachers and healthcare professionals must contribute towards building an accessible, equitable, scientifically responsible and responsive healthcare system. She expressed confidence that this National Convention will encourage scientific dialogue, promote institutional partnerships and inspire a new generation of competent, ethical and socially responsible healthcare professionals.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Vice-President Unveils Life-size Bronze Statue of Late Shri Jawaharlal Darda in Yavatmal
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Vice President's Secretariat 
 Vice-President Unveils Life-size Bronze Statue of Late Shri Jawaharlal Darda in Yavatmal 
 Late Shri Jawaharlal Darda Made Lasting Contributions to Maharashtra’s Industrial Development and Public Welfare: Vice-President Shivaji Maharaj Restored National Self-Respect, Dr. Ambedkar Gave India Its Constitution and Tilak Awakened Patriotism: Vice-President Cooperative Institutions Play a Vital Role in Strengthening Rural Economy and Empowering Farmers: Vice-President 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today unveiled the life-size bronze statue of Late Shri Jawaharlal Darda, freedom fighter, statesman, journalist and Founder of Lokmat Media Group, at Priyadarshini Sahakari Soot Girni, Yavatmal, Maharashtra. 
 Earlier, the Vice-President visited Prerna Sthal in Yavatmal and offered floral tributes to Late Shri Jawaharlal Darda. 
Paying his tributes, the Vice-President described Babuji’s life as a remarkable journey of patriotism, public service and commitment to society. Recalling his contribution to India’s freedom struggle, particularly the Quit India Movement of 1942, he said that Babuji continued to serve the nation after Independence as a statesman, public representative, minister and journalist. He highlighted his contributions to Maharashtra’s development, national unity and communal harmony.
The Vice-President noted that Late Shri Darda made significant contributions across several sectors, including industry, energy, housing, education, healthcare, agriculture and cooperation. He particularly recalled his landmark Industrial Policy of 1993, which promoted balanced industrial development across different regions of Maharashtra. He also highlighted Babuji’s contribution to the establishment of the Government Medical College in Yavatmal, reflecting his commitment to extending development opportunities to every region.
Highlighting Babuji’s vision of rural development, the Vice-President said that the Priyadarshini Sahakari Soot Girni exemplifies the important link between cotton cultivation, textile manufacturing, employment generation and rural prosperity. He appreciated the farmers, cooperative members, management and workers for their collective efforts in reviving the institution from financial difficulties. He emphasised that cooperative institutions have an important role in strengthening the rural economy and empowering farmers.
Drawing upon his own association with the textile sector, the Vice-President highlighted the sector’s immense potential for employment generation and economic growth. Referring to India’s growing international trade opportunities, he expressed optimism about the future of textile exports and called for modernisation of mills, machinery, weaving, dyeing and printing facilities to enhance the sector’s competitiveness.
The Vice-President also recalled Maharashtra’s distinguished contributions to India’s national life through great personalities such as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He said that their contributions to national self-respect, constitutional values and the spirit of patriotism continue to inspire the country.
Calling for renewed commitment to Babuji’s ideals, the Vice-President urged all stakeholders to strengthen the cooperative movement, empower farmers and create meaningful employment opportunities in rural India. He said that the legacy of Late Shri Jawaharlal Darda should continue to inspire collective efforts towards inclusive development.
The occasion was attended by Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, Governor of Maharashtra; Shri Chandrakant Patil, Minister for Textiles and Higher and Technical Education, Maharashtra; Shri Sanjay Rathod, Minister for Soil and Water Conservation, Maharashtra; Dr. Vijay Darda, Chairman, Lokmat Media Group and former Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha; Shri Rajendra Darda, former Cabinet Minister and Editor-in-Chief, Lokmat Media Group; Shri Kirti Gandhi, Vice-President, Priyadarshini Co-operative Spinning Mill Ltd.; members of the Darda family, representatives of the cooperative sector, farmers, workers and other dignitaries.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Vice-President Inaugurates Swayamsiddha National Conference 2026 on Women’s Empowerment in Nagpur
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Vice President's Secretariat 
 Vice-President Inaugurates Swayamsiddha National Conference 2026 on Women’s Empowerment in Nagpur 
 Respect for Women and Their Leadership Is Deeply Rooted in Indian Civilisation: Vice-President Women’s Empowerment Is a Shared Responsibility of Government, Universities and Society: Vice-President Women’s Empowerment Must Move from Education to Leadership: Vice-President 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the Swayamsiddha National Conference 2026 on Women’s Empowerment, themed “VIJAYA – A Journey of Empowerment through Education”, organised by the Swayamsiddha Centre of Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University in Nagpur, Maharashtra. 
 Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President recalled initiating the Swayamsiddha programme during his tenure as Governor of Maharashtra and appreciated its continued expansion under the leadership of the present Governor, Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, with universities across Maharashtra participating in its activities. He emphasised that universities must go beyond imparting academic qualifications and actively contribute to women’s empowerment by promoting skills, economic independence, confidence and leadership.
Highlighting the growing participation of women in higher education, the Vice-President observed that, at convocations across the country, women students increasingly outnumber men among gold medallists. Referring to the All India Survey on Higher Education, he noted that the female Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education had increased significantly over the last decade. He said this progress reflected the expanding opportunities for women and the country’s transition from women’s development to women-led development.
Referring to the forthcoming Constitution Day, the Vice-President recalled the contributions of 15 women members of the Constituent Assembly to the framing of the Constitution of India. He also highlighted the significance of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in advancing women’s representation in democratic institutions.
Emphasising India’s cultural ethos, the Vice-President said that respect for women and their leadership is deeply rooted in Indian civilisation. He called upon educational institutions to prepare young women for leadership roles across all spheres of life. He stressed that education must open pathways for women to participate in research, entrepreneurship, administration, public life and institutional decision-making, with particular attention to those from rural, remote and economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
The Vice-President emphasised that women’s empowerment was a shared responsibility of governments, universities, industry, civil society and families. He expressed hope that the proposed Maharashtra–VIJAYA Framework for Women in Higher Education would provide a basis for sustained institutional action.
Congratulating the University for bringing Swayamsiddha to the national platform, the Vice-President expressed hope that the VIJAYA conference would facilitate meaningful discussions, innovative solutions and practical recommendations. He said that the success of Swayamsiddha would ultimately be reflected in the confidence, independence and leadership of the women it reaches.
On the occasion, the Vice-President unveiled the Swayamsiddha logo and released two compendiums—Hundred Voices of Young Women and Best Practices in Higher Education. He also felicitated Swayamsiddha leaders in recognition of their contributions to the initiative and joined the participants in taking the ‘No to Drugs’ pledge. 
 The event was attended by Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, Governor of Maharashtra; Dr. Manali Kshirsagar, Vice-Chancellor, Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University; Dr. Prashant Narnaware, IAS, Secretary to the Governor of Maharashtra; Dr. Akhilesh Peshwe, Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University; representatives of the National Commission for Women and Maharashtra State Commission for Women; academicians, faculty members, officers and students.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs. 1,491 crore
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Cabinet 
 Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs. 1,491 crore 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Department of Posts for the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme, the Estates Management Scheme, during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year period. 
 Strategic Objective: 
 The scheme aims to comprehensively transform and modernize the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts. It focuses heavily on the construction, re-construction, renovation, uniform branding of post offices and residential colonies, along with the preservation of India’s heritage postal buildings. This modernization strategy directly supports first-mile delivery, fosters financial inclusion and enhances citizen centric service delivery nationwide, aligning with the broader visions of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. 
 As one of the world's largest postal networks with 1.65 lakh post offices (including 1,49,385 in rural areas), India Post remains a critical vehicle for mails, banking (POSB/IPPB), insurance (PLI), Aadhaar services, Post Office Passport Seva Kendras and rural artisan support via Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). 
 Implementation Timeline: 
 The scheme is scheduled for phased implementation over a five-year horizon, starting from FY 2026-27 through FY 2030-31. 
 Key Components of the Approved Scheme: 
 New Construction (Rs. 280 Crore): Building 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant departmental plots to replace currently rented spaces and eliminate rental liabilities. 
 Re-construction (Rs. 108 Crore): Demolishing and rebuilding 50 dilapidated departmental postal structures to ensure long-term structural safety. 
 Renovation & Branding (Rs. 318 Crore): Upgrading and establishing uniform branding across 2,550 departmental SubPost Offices as per SPA guidelines. 
 Rented Post Office Upgrades (Rs. 37.50 Crore): Upgrading and uniformly branding 2,500 post offices operating out of rented premises. 
 Heritage Preservation (Rs. 180 Crore): Restoring and preserving 20 landmark heritage postal buildings to safeguard the historical legacy of the department. 
 Colony Renovation (Rs. 357.50 Crore): Revamping 150 high demand postal residential colonies to elevate employee welfare and satisfaction. 
 Allied & Inclusive Activities (Rs. 100 Crore): Implementing sustainable features (Solar power, Rainwater Harvesting) and universal accessibility infrastructure (ramps, Braille signage) under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, alongwith gender-focused additions like ladies toilets and feeding rooms. 
 Integrated Technology Center (Rs. 100 Crore): Setting up a permanent physical infrastructure for the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) in Bengaluru to drive Advanced Postal Technology (APT) services and support the indigenous Opensource Tech Stack.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cabinet approves continuation of Postal Operations Scheme with an outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore for 16th Finance Commission Cycle (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31)
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Cabinet 
 Cabinet approves continuation of Postal Operations Scheme with an outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore for 16th Finance Commission Cycle (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31) 
 The scheme aims to modernize postal network, strengthen parcel and mail operations, enhance rural connectivity and improve citizen-centric services Focus on e-commerce logistics, financial inclusion, international mail operations and digital transformation of India Post services 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme “Postal Operations” during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with a proposed outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore. The scheme seeks to strengthen postal infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and support the growing requirements of logistics, e-commerce and digital service delivery across the country. 
 With one of the world’s largest postal networks comprising 1.65 lakh post offices, including 1,49,655 post offices in rural areas, India Post continues to serve as an important platform for delivery of mail, parcels, banking, insurance and other citizen-centric services, particularly in remote and underserved regions. 
 Apart from its core postal operations, India Post provides a wide range of public services through initiatives such as Post Office Savings Bank (POSB), India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), Postal Life Insurance (PLI), Aadhaar enrolment and updation, Passport Services through Post Office Passport Seva Kendras, KYC verification services and support to rural artisans through Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). 
 The scheme would support modernization of postal infrastructure, strengthen last-mile delivery, improve logistics efficiency, promote financial inclusion and enhance customer-centric service delivery across the country. The proposal also aligns with the broader objectives of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. 
 The scheme is intended to be implemented over a period of five years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. 
 The Postal Operations Scheme comprises the following six sub-schemes: 
 Rural Business and Access to Postal Network – Rs. 120 crore – Focused on infrastructure upgrades, standardized branding and better resource utilization to transform post offices, particularly in rural areas, into efficient and citizen-centric service hubs. The component aims to strengthen financial inclusion, digital connectivity and local economic development while improving last-mile delivery and enhancing access to postal and citizen-centric services in underserved regions. 
 Mail Network Optimization – Rs. 575 crore – Envisages modernization of mail operations through centralized delivery systems, mechanization, advanced IT solutions under Advanced Postal Technology (APT 2.0), GIS-based services and upgraded infrastructure. The initiative also includes strengthening delivery post offices, mail handling systems, Mail Motor Service (MMS) workshops, Road Transport Network and modern smart 24x7 letter boxes to improve operational efficiency, transparency, service quality and logistical reliability across the network. 
 Parcel Network Optimization – Rs. 278 crore – Includes construction of Parcel Hubs and expansion of Parcel Packaging Units (PPUs) aligned with the redesigned sorting framework to streamline parcel movement, reduce handling points, ease capacity constraints and improve transit times. The component also aims to support growing parcel volumes from e-commerce and rural markets through purpose-built facilities, standardized secure packaging and enhanced operational flexibility while improving customer trust and strengthening India Post’s competitiveness in the logistics sector. 
 Infrastructure Upgrade and Augmentation of Infrastructure for International Mails – Rs. 8 crore – Aims to strengthen international mail services by upgrading Foreign Post Offices (FPOs) and Sub Foreign Post Offices (SFPOs) to improve infrastructure and expedite processing of international consignments. The initiative also includes marketing and Advertisement through Postal / RMS Division and position India Post as a reliable international logistics provider while improving compliance, technology integration and export logistics support. 
 Marketing Functions including Quality of Service – Rs. 100 crore – Focused on promotion, branding, outreach and customer engagement through multi-channel campaigns across television, digital, radio, print and outdoor platforms. The component also includes participation in events and exhibitions, social media campaigns, direct marketing and expansion of Dak Chaupal activities to deepen grassroots engagement, especially in rural and underserved areas. In addition, it envisages infrastructure upgrades, studio facilities, ICT enhancements, market research, influencer engagement and third-party evaluation mechanisms to improve quality of service and strengthen a customer-centric approach. 
 Philately Operations – Rs. 60 crore – Proposes initiatives to promote philately through exhibitions, seminars, quizzes, school philatelic clubs and innovative stamp designs including scented, holographic and 3D stamps. The component also includes digital outreach activities, programmes such as the Dhai Akhar letter-writing competition and SPARSH scholarship, modernization of production and fulfillment centres, market research and international collaboration with the objective of revitalizing philately as an engaging educational and cultural activity while also improving operational efficiency and revenue potential.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cabinet approves Rs.11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Cabinet 
 Cabinet approves Rs.11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem 
 The scheme aims to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment ecosystem in India, supporting the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the "Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem" with a financial outlay of Rs.11,000 crore. The Scheme, to be implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), aims to incentivize domestic manufacturing of CIE and its components and to establish a dedicated CIE testing facility in the country, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the Global CIE market. 
 India's CIE industry is currently the world's third largest, after China and the United States, with a market size of around Rs.97,500 crore in FY2024-25. Driven by accelerated growth in infrastructure (roads and ports) and housing, the industry is projected to increase more than double, reaching a market size of around Rs.2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30. 
 Driven by rapid growth in the construction and infrastructure sector, the scheme aims to incentivize manufacturing of technologically advanced equipment such as Ship-to-Shore Cranes, Tunnel Boring Machines, Hydraulic Excavators, Off-Highway Trucks, etc. The scheme has also provision of establishment of state of art dedicated CIE testing facility in the country. 
 The scheme with duration of eight years from FY2026-27, comprise of a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) for setting up manufacturing facilities, followed by a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33), and a final year (FY2033-34) for settlement of incentives on incremental sales of FY2032-33. 
 The scheme has two components: 
 Sales-linked Incentive – Incentives will be provided on the Incremental Sales Value of eligible CIE equipment and components to approved applicants across two categories – eligible OEMs and Component Manufacturers. Graded Incentive rates range from 13% to 8% of incremental sales value over a five-year period. 
 Grant for CIE Testing Facility – A grant of up to Rs.375 crore , in the nature of Viability Gap Funding, for setting up a dedicated CIE testing facility, 
 This initiative by the Government of India is a landmark step towards strengthening the domestic Construction and Infrastructure Equipment manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in the global markets. By fostering indigenous capabilities in manufacturing of CIE, the scheme will ensure supply chain security, increase opportunities for employment and promote Atmanirbhar Bharat. It embodies the Government’s unwavering commitment to build a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive and sustainable industrial base, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cabinet approves development of Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam at an estimated cost of 2,014 crore
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) 
 Cabinet approves development of Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam at an estimated cost of 2,014 crore 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi 
 To overcome the severe operational and spatial constraints of the existing defense landlocked civil enclave at Silchar Airport and to accommodate sustained passenger growth, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the development of a New Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at an estimated cost of Rs.2,014 crore. 
 Doloo, situated in the Cachar District of Assam, serves as the strategic heart of the Barak Valley—a region renowned for its extensive tea gardens, agro-based industries, and immense potential for eco and cultural tourism. 
 The proposed Terminal Building will span a total area of 12,351 sqm with a capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hour, designed with modern passenger amenities, sustainable green building principles, and modular expansion capability. In addition, the project encompasses the development of a 2,705m x 45m, Code-4C compliant runway suitable for A-320 aircraft operations, along with the construction of a new Apron capable of parking 6 nos. A-320 aircraft and a dedicated isolation bay. 
 As a project of immense strategic significance, the Doloo Greenfield Airport will meet the rapidly growing demands of air traffic in South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring States. It will significantly decongest existing infrastructure, unlock regional economic potential by boosting trade and tourism, and offer a world-class gateway integrating Northeast India with broader national and international growth corridors.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cabinet approves development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) Basis
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) 
 Cabinet approves development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) Basis 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposed project for development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL) under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis, at an estimated project cost of Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST. The project envisages the development of a 900-metre-long container terminal with a design draft of 18 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs), to be implemented in two phases. 
 Expenditure involved: 
 The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The investment is to be arranged by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. The project proposal separately indicates an estimated dredging cost of Rs.450 crore to be borne by KPL. 
 Details: 
 (i) The project envisages development of a 900-metre-long Second Container Terminal with a berth width of 30 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million TEUs. The terminal will be developed in two phases: Phase I with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs and Phase II with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs. 
 (ii) The terminal is designed to handle large container vessels, including vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length overall, with a design draft of 18 metres. This will strengthen KPL’s ability to handle larger mainline vessels and improve connectivity with international shipping routes. 
 (iii) The project is intended to meet the growing demand for containerised export-import (EXIM) cargo from the Chennai–Ennore industrial and economic region and the wider southern hinterland. Key cargo-generating sectors include automobiles and auto components, engineering goods, electronics, chemicals and other manufactured products. 
 (iv) KPL handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26, including more than 7 lakh TEUs of container traffic. The existing container terminal has an installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs per annum and handled approximately 0.7 million TEUs in FY 2025–26, representing utilisation of about 88%. 
 (v) Container traffic in India has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 7% over the last five years, while KPL’s container traffic has grown at approximately 9.9% during the same period. The feasibility study projects continued growth in container traffic in the south-eastern region, supporting the need to augment capacity at KPL. 
 (vi) The project will be implemented on a DBFOT basis for a concession period of 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months. Phase I is scheduled for completion within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, with commercial operations commencing in the 25th month. Construction of Phase II will be undertaken from the 25th to the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month. 
 (vii) The estimated project cost is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The cost is to be financed by the selected concessionaire through the DBFOT framework. In addition, KPL is to incur an estimated Rs.450 crore towards dredging, as indicated in the project proposal. 
 (viii) The project is proposed to be implemented through a transparent, open global bidding process. The concessionaire will arrange the required financing and recover its investment through user charges in accordance with the provisions of the Concession Agreement and applicable tariff framework. 
 (ix) The project is aligned with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. It is expected to strengthen KPL’s position as a container gateway on India’s East Coast, improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics chain and support the growth of EXIM trade. 
 Implementation Strategy and Targets: 
 The project will be implemented by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. Phase I, with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs, is to be completed within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, and commercial operations are to commence in the 25th month. Phase II, with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs, is to be completed by the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month. The project proposal also provides for obtaining environmental and other necessary clearances in a time-bound manner before the bid due date. 
 Major Impact: 
 (i) The additional capacity of 2.0 million TEUs per annum will strengthen KPL’s ability to accommodate growing container traffic and provide an additional gateway for EXIM cargo from the industrial clusters of Tamil Nadu and the adjoining hinterland. 
 (ii) The terminal’s design draft of 18 metres and capability to handle large container vessels are expected to improve international connectivity, facilitate direct calls by mainline vessels and reduce dependence on foreign deep-water hub ports and associated feedering costs. 
 (iii) The project is expected to improve maritime logistics efficiency, support trade and manufacturing, strengthen the port’s revenue potential and contribute to India’s maritime competitiveness. 
 (iv) The project is expected to generate employment for approximately 750 persons directly and indirectly during construction and to increase about 800 persons during the operational phase.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cabinet Approves MoU with Republic of Singapore for Aviation MRO
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Civil Aviation 
 Cabinet Approves MoU with Republic of Singapore for Aviation MRO 
 MoU to Strengthen Maintenance Skilling and Facilitate Development of MRO Facilities 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Union Cabinet, chaired by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Government of India and the Republic of Singapore on “Cooperation in Skills and Industry Development within the Aviation Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Sector (MRO)”. 
 Welcoming the decision, Union Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu said, “This MoU between India and Singapore will be highly impactful and is closely aligned with Hon’ble PM’s vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. We want to see every aircraft component including the landing gear, the radomes, engines, cockpit displays, seats, wings and smallest of the parts getting repaired in India. And the objective of this MoU is also to position India as the regional aviation workshop”. 
 Highlighting the potential of the India-Singapore partnership, the Minister further added, “Singapore has a well-established aviation MRO ecosystem, while India is among the world's fastest-growing aviation markets. With our expanding aircraft fleet, strategic geographical position as a regional aviation hub and the Government's continued efforts to improve the ease of doing business, India offers significant opportunities for the growth of the MRO sector.” 
 The proposed cooperation will enable Indian training institutions to strengthen their curriculum and training capabilities through knowledge exchange and industry exposure. The initiative is also expected to contribute to the development of domestic MRO infrastructure through greater industry participation and over time, reduce India's dependence on overseas maintenance services. 
 The MoU will provide a framework for facilitating the exchange of knowledge, expertise and best practices between the two countries. 
 Key provisions of the MoU include: 
 Joint development of an industry-oriented curriculum for Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME) training. 
 Sharing of expertise and capacity building of Indian institutes to ensure quality delivery of the curriculum. 
 Internship and exchange programs with Singapore MRO entities, enabling Indian students to gain practical industry experience. 
 Facilitation of partnerships between Indian and Singaporean industry stakeholders to support the expansion of MRO facilities 
 Talking about India’s MRO requirements, Shri Ram Mohan Naidu mentioned , “India is witnessing unprecedented growth in air traffic, with airlines steadily expanding their aircraft fleets. This has created an increasing demand for domestic MRO capabilities and skilled Aircraft Maintenance Engineers. Strengthening our domestic MRO ecosystem is now the need of the hour. Dependence on overseas maintenance services often results in higher costs and longer aircraft downtime for our airlines. This strategic MoU will enable us to meet our own growing requirements for skilled AMEs and advanced MRO facilities. It will also be a milestone decision to develop India in global aviation skilling as well as MRO destination for global airlines.” 
 The MoU marks another important step towards strengthening India's aviation ecosystem, creating skilled employment opportunities for its youth and advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat in the aviation MRO sector. 
 *** 
 Divyanshu Kumar

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: DPIIT Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata and Reduction of Pendency
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
 DPIIT Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata and Reduction of Pendency 
 Biomass Gasifier Installed at NCCBM’s Ballabgarh Campus to Promote Sustainable Waste-to-Energy Conversion DPIIT Achieves 100% Disposal of Public Grievances Under Special Campaign 6, Reclaims 18,644 Sq. Ft. of Office Space 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 1:39PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, concluded Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign, aimed at institutionalising the principles of Swachhata (cleanliness) and minimising pendency in official work, was undertaken across all offices to promote cleanliness, efficiency and effective record management. 
 Special Campaign 6 was conducted from 2nd of October to 31st of October 2026, preceded by a preparatory phase from 15th of September to 30th September 2026. Throughout the campaign, DPIIT undertook focused efforts to promote awareness about cleanliness, systematic record management and the timely disposal of pending cases. With near-total achievement of the identified targets and notable progress across various campaign parameters, DPIIT reaffirmed its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, fostering a culture of efficiency and responsiveness, and strengthening sustainable practices in government functioning. 
 As part of the campaign, the National Council for Cement and Building Materials (NCCBM), an autonomous organisation under DPIIT, installed a biomass gasifier at its Ballabgarh campus in Haryana. The gasifier uses biomass, wood and refuse-derived fuel (RDF) as feedstock to produce a combustible gas known as Syngas. During the campaign, NCCBM successfully conducted a trial run using 150 kg of dry horticultural waste. The waste was first shredded and subsequently converted into Syngas through partial oxidation at elevated temperatures under a controlled supply of gasifying agents. The potential utilisation of the Syngas generated through this process in power generation and diesel generator (DG) sets will be explored further. Trial runs using Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) obtained from Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) were also conducted in the gasifier during the campaign. This initiative showcases an environmentally sustainable approach to waste-to-energy conversion and offers a replicable model for promoting sustainable infrastructure, resource recovery and the principles of a circular economy. 
 In addition to this initiative, DPIIT made significant progress across other key parameters of the campaign. Its attached and subordinate offices undertook the disposal of scrap materials and e-waste, resulting in the reclamation of 18,644 square feet of office space and the generation of ₹16,52,569 in revenue. The Department also achieved 100% completion in the disposal of public grievances and nearly 100% completion across other key parameters, including public grievance appeals, review of e-files and physical files, and cleanliness activities. Special attention was also given to improving the overall workplace environment to enhance employee comfort and productivity. These efforts reflect DPIIT's continued emphasis on accountability, efficient record management and the timely resolution of pending matters. 
 *** 
 Abhishek Dayal/ C N Abhijith Narayanan/ Abhimanyu Panwar

Ministry of Communications 
 TRAI releases findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Noida, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and nearby areas route under Delhi LSA, for the month of Sep 2026 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Noida, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and nearby areas route under Delhi LSA, during the month of Sep 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. 
 These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems. 
 TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 813.4 Km, Hotspot locations - 08, Walk Test – 3.8 Km, Inter Operator Calling at 01 location during 01 st Sep 2026 to 05 th Sep 2026 in Delhi LSA . These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test. 
 Drive Test Route Map : The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots & walk test as per the legends shown on the map: - 
 Figure-1: Drive test routes 
 Key Parameters Assessed 
 a) Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G). 
 b) Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS). 
 c) Call Silence Instance : Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls. 
 d) Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate. 
 The overall mobile network performance across Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida (Delhi LSA) for the key Parameters has been summarized below: 
 a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1053/127346 for Airtel, 79985/121733 for BSNL/MTNL, 2146/127212 for RJIL & 1246/132094 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure -I . 
 b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 9/1139 for Airtel, 173/1071 for BSNL/MTNL, 14/1146 for RJIL & 2/1158 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure -I . 
 c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 8/1086 for Airtel, 10/878 for BSNL/MTNL, 54/1086 for RJIL & 4/1107 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure -I .

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Over 1,100 Students Complete Five-Day ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ Under Somnath Swabhiman Parv; Return to New Delhi
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Culture 
 Over 1,100 Students Complete Five-Day ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ Under Somnath Swabhiman Parv; Return to New Delhi 
 Students visit Somnath temples, pilgrimage sites and historical landmarks to understand India's rich cultural and spiritual heritage 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi 
 The five-day ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’, organised under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv from 20 to 25 November 2026, concluded with the return of more than 1,100 students to Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi. During the journey, the participants visited various temples, pilgrimage sites and historical landmarks in Somnath, gaining a closer understanding of India's rich spiritual and cultural heritage. 
 The journey began on 20 November when Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat flagged off the special train from Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi. The train reached Veraval Railway Station in Gujarat on 21 November, where the students received a vibrant traditional welcome with folk dance performances and flower showers. 
 On 22 November, the students visited Shri Ram Temple at Prabhas Patan, Golokdham Tirth and the revered first Jyotirlinga, Shri Somnath Mahadev Temple. They also attended the ‘Jai Somnath’ Light and Sound Show at the Somnath Temple, which presented the temple's rich history and its enduring significance. 
 On 23 November, the youngsters visited Baan Ganga, Bhidbhanjan Mahadev Temple, Bhalka Tirth and Ahilyabai Temple. They also visited the museum and the Swadeshi Haat, where they got an opportunity to learn about local culture and indigenous products. The day's activities concluded with students experiencing the divine Aarti at Triveni Ghat. 
 On 24 November, the students departed from Veraval Railway Station for New Delhi by the special train. The journey concluded on 25 November with their arrival at Safdarjung Railway Station, where they received a warm welcome. 
 The five-day journey offered students an opportunity to experience the religious and historical significance of Somnath and understand the resilience of India's cultural heritage. Sharing their experiences, participants described the Yatra as more than a spiritual journey, calling it a memorable experience that brought them closer to India's culture, heritage and history. 
 The Somnath Swabhiman Parv is being organised to mark 1,000 years since the first recorded attack on the Somnath Temple. As part of the celebrations, special journeys are being organised to connect devotees and visitors from different parts of the country with the spiritual and cultural heritage of Somnath. More than 35,000 people have so far visited Somnath Mahadev through these initiatives. 
 The ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ was part of this broader initiative, aimed at connecting the younger generation with India's historical legacy, cultural values and rich heritage. Through such initiatives, the Ministry of Culture continues to encourage young people to learn about and engage with the country's diverse cultural traditions and historical landmarks. 
 *** 
 M Annadurai

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: INDIA–NEPAL JOINT MILITARY EXERCISE ‘SURYAKIRAN XX’ COMMENCES IN NEPAL
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Defence 
 INDIA–NEPAL JOINT MILITARY EXERCISE ‘SURYAKIRAN XX’ COMMENCES IN NEPAL 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi 
 The 20th edition of the India–Nepal Joint Military Exercise SURYAKIRAN commenced today at the Nepal Army Battle School, Saljhandi, Nepal. The exercise is scheduled to be conducted from 25 November to 08 December 2026. The Opening Ceremony was graced by Major General Purna Bahadur Khatri, General Officer Commanding, Mid Western Division, Nepal Army. The Indian Army contingent, comprising 334 personnel, is being represented by troops from the KUMAON Regiment. The Nepal Army contingent, comprising an equal number of personnel, is being represented by troops from Shri Jawla Dal Battalion. 
 The aim of the exercise is to enhance interoperability, operational coordination and mutual understanding between the two Armies through joint training in counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations in challenging terrain. 
 The scope of the exercise includes joint tactical operations, heliborne operations, disaster response and medical training. Troops from both Armies will exchange operational experiences and best practices while refining tactics, techniques and procedures to enhance joint operational effectiveness. 
 Exercise SURYAKIRAN is an annual bilateral military exercise conducted alternately in India and Nepal. The exercise will further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation, foster mutual trust and camaraderie between the two Armies and reaffirm the shared commitment of both nations towards regional peace, stability and security. 
 ***** 
 Nishant / Ashish

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Aero India 2027: Record exhibitor demand prompts major capacity expansion by Ministry of Defence
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Defence 
 Aero India 2027: Record exhibitor demand prompts major capacity expansion by Ministry of Defence 
 Two new exhibition hangars under construction; Mezzanine floors permitted for the first time to accommodate maximum industry participation 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi 
 In response to the significant rise in global and domestic exhibitor demand, the Department of Defence Production (DDP), Ministry of Defence, has initiated major infrastructure expansions for Aero India 2027. Scheduled to be held at Air Force Station Yelahanka, Bengaluru from February 8 to 12, 2027, the 16th edition of Asia’s largest air show and one of the world’s premier aerospace & defence exhibitions has witnessed exhibition space requests exceed initial capacity by approximately 12,000 sq. metres - a testament to India’s rapidly maturing aerospace and defence ecosystem. 
 Operating within the strict aviation safety and operational parameters of an active Indian Air Force training base limits horizontal expansion at the Yelahanka venue. To overcome these spatial constraints and accommodate the maximum possible number of exhibitors, DDP has rolled out two key solutions: 
 Construction of Two Additional Hangars : Two brand-new exhibition hangars are being built to significantly expand overall floor capacity. 
 First-ever Permission for Mezzanine Floors : To optimise vertical space without increasing the ground footprint, exhibitors will, for the first time in Aero India’s history, be permitted to construct mezzanine floors within their allotted stalls, wherever hangar height permits. All mezzanine structures will strictly adhere to prescribed structural stability, load-bearing, and safety standards. 
 The DDP aims to ensure that global aerospace leaders, domestic manufacturers, and innovators have ample opportunity to showcase their cutting-edge capabilities and technologies at Aero India 2027. 
 ***** 
 SR/Savvy

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Operation Drishti: AFMS doctors perform record 412 sight-restoring surgeries during surgical eye camp at Military Hospital, Meerut
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Defence 
 Operation Drishti: AFMS doctors perform record 412 sight-restoring surgeries during surgical eye camp at Military Hospital, Meerut 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi 
 A total of 412 sight-restoring surgeries have been conducted free of cost by an expert team of doctors of Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) during a surgical eye camp at Military Hospital, Meerut under Operation Drishti. The five-day camp, which concluded on November 25, 2026, brought a new lease of light to people across the region, including 197 underprivileged civilians, who underwent surgeries for cataract, glaucoma, vitreo-retinal and pterygium. The special highlight was the successful surgeries of approximately 60 mature cataract patients who were completely blind. 
 Over the past two months, more than 12,000 patients were screened by ophthalmologists and medical officers of AFMS for cataract and other eye ailments at Bagpat, Bulandshahar, Hapur, Shamli and Moradabad, ensuring that even residents of distant towns and villages were reached. Close to 5,000 patients were screened during the camp at Military Hospital, Meerut. Patients found in need of surgery were brought to the Military Hospital where 412 surgeries were performed between 22nd & 24th November 2026. 
 The closing ceremony of the camp was graced by Minister of State, Sainik Kalyan Vikas Nigam and PRD, Uttar Pradesh Dr Somendra Tomar as the Chief Guest. He interacted with patients and members of the medical team, appreciating the efforts of the Indian Army towards extending a helping hand to civilians on a large scale. 
 Speaking on the occasion, DGAFMS Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja commended the medical team for its outstanding contribution and setting a new benchmark in professional excellence, dedicated service and compassionate patient care. AFMS is focusing not only on veterans and the dependents of serving personnel; but also the civilian population who do not have access to such facilities, he said. 
 412 surgeries are the highest-ever in any previous eye camp, setting a new benchmark in delivering quality healthcare and compassionate service. The surgeries were performed by an expert team of doctors from Army Hospital (Research & Referral), led by Head of Department (Ophthalmology) Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, who is spearheading Operation Drishti, the series of mega surgical eye camps that carries advanced eye care to remote and underserved regions of the country. The camp was organised under the aegis of HQ Surya Command.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Union Education Minister, Shri Pralhad Joshi chairs the Meeting of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee on Internationalisation of Indian Education
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Education 
 Union Education Minister, Shri Pralhad Joshi chairs the Meeting of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee on Internationalisation of Indian Education 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi 
 Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, today chaired the first meeting of the Consultative Committee of the Parliament for the Ministry of Education for 2026. Union Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary; Secretary, Department of Higher Education, Ms. Deepti Gaur Mukerjee; Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar and other senior officials from the Ministry attended the meeting. 
 Addressing the meeting, Shri Pralhad Joshi said that the Indian Knowledge System had a long history of global impact. The objective of the Ministry was to further expand the global footprint of this system. With this aim, he stated that several steps were being taken to set up campuses of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) overseas and also facilitate the setting up of campuses of foreign universities in India. The Minister informed that around 21 foreign HEIs were currently operational in the country, in addition to joint academic and research collaborations. He added that the demand for CBSE schools abroad demonstrated the credibility of Indian education programmes and their potential for scalability at the global level. 
 The Members of the Parliament were briefed on the various initiatives undertaken by both the Departments of the Ministry as part of the internationalisation of Indian education. The Department of Higher Education outlined the four strategies adopted to promote internationalisation - academic and research collaborations; attracting international students to study in India; allowing Foreign HEIs (FHEIs) to set up branch campuses in India; and allowing Indian HEIs to set up campuses abroad. 17 Letters of Intent were issued to Foreign Universities, under UGC Regulations, including those from the UK, the USA, Australia and Italy. The Members were also briefed on initiatives including Bharat Innovates, SPARC (Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration), GIAN (Global Initiative of Academic Networks) and DASA (Direct Admission of Students Abroad) and the revamped Study in India (SII) portal. 
 The Department of School Education and Literacy informed the Members that the National Education Policy 2020 and the aspiration of Viksit Bharat 2047 were guiding a transformative shift in the Indian education system. The alignment of the curriculum with global standards, multilingual education, exchange programmes for students and teachers and the PARAKH National Assessment Centre for academic equivalence and quality alignment were among the key factors driving internationalisation. 268 CBSE schools were functional across 26 countries and an overseas regional office was also established in Dubai. A standardised assessment framework had also been implemented across affiliated schools globally to ensure uniformity. 
 The Members appreciated the efforts taken by the Departments in the direction of internationalisation and gave their suggestions on various matters including vocational education and expanding the network of Indian educational institutions abroad.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry Records ₹4,385.28 Crore Incentive Disbursement in FY 2026–27
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Heavy Industries 
 PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry Records ₹4,385.28 Crore Incentive Disbursement in FY 2026–27 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:56PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) continues to strengthen India's automobile and auto component manufacturing ecosystem through the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry. The scheme aims to enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, promote advanced automotive technologies and position India as a global hub for automobile manufacturing. 
 Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, Shri H. D. Kumaraswamy, chaired a review meeting with Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), today to review the progress and implementation of the PLI-Auto Scheme. 
 Accelerated Incentive Disbursement under the PLI-Auto Scheme 
 With a total approved budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore, the PLI-Auto Scheme has made significant progress in promoting investments, strengthening domestic supply chains and encouraging the manufacturing of Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products. During FY 2026–27, incentive disbursements under the scheme reached ₹4,385.28 crore as of 25 th November 2026. The cumulative incentive disbursement under the scheme since its inception has reached ₹6,771.64 crore. 
 Strong Investment, Incremental Sales and Employment Generation 
 The scheme has also recorded encouraging progress in attracting investments and generating employment. As of 30 th September 2026, approved applicants had reported cumulative investments of ₹52,806 crore, surpassing the targeted investment of ₹42,500 crore. The scheme has also facilitated incremental sales of ₹82,993 crore over the base year FY 2019–20 and generated 77,755 employment opportunities, reflecting its contribution to strengthening India's automotive manufacturing ecosystem. 
 Strengthening Domestic Manufacturing and Value Addition 
 Promoting domestic value addition remains a key objective of the PLI-Auto Scheme. The scheme mandates a minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for eligible products to qualify for incentives. As of 25 th November 2026, DVA certificates have been issued to 9 Champion OEMs covering 139 products/variants, and 10 Component Champions covering 53 products/variants. This progress reflects the growing domestic capabilities in manufacturing advanced automotive products and components. 
 The initiative is aligned with the Government of India's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, reinforcing the country's commitment to becoming a leading global destination for automobile and auto component manufacturing. The Ministry of Heavy Industries remains committed to supporting the growth of a robust, resilient and technologically advanced automotive industry through sustained policy initiatives and industry collaboration.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Ego We Reach All Explores Street Childhood, Identity and Resilience in Ghana; Filmmakers Highlight the Potential of International Collaborations 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:01PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 The team behind Ego We Reach All (Our Time Will Come), an international co-production from Ghana, France and Saudi Arabia, interacted with the media today at the Press Conference Hall on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Panaji, Goa. Screened under the International Cinema section, the 104-minute feature is celebrating its Asia Premiere at the festival. 
 Director Amartei Armar and Producer Yemoh Ike shared insights into the film’s creative journey, its exploration of childhood and survival on the streets of Ghana and the importance of international collaborations in bringing locally rooted stories to audiences across the world. 
 Speaking about the film’s thematic inspiration, Director Amartei Armar said he has long been fascinated by street childhood in Ghana and the stories of young people navigating life on the margins. The film, he said, seeks to explore how stories of those often overlooked by society can be brought into the larger national and cinematic discourse. Through the narrative, the filmmakers seek to affirm that young people from diverse circumstances are equally part of the country and its future. 
 Reflecting on his filmmaking journey and his continued connection with Ghana, Armar emphasized the need for filmmakers to take ownership of their stories and make their voices heard. He noted that independent filmmakers often work within financial constraints, making it imperative to create films that demonstrate cinematic quality and storytelling potential to attract investors and strengthen the industry. 
 Highlighting the scope for cultural exchange between India and Ghana, the filmmakers drew parallels between the cinematic cultures of the two countries, citing Ghana’s ‘Ghallywood’ as a counterpart to India’s Bollywood. They noted that audiences in both countries could find cultural resonances in each other’s storytelling traditions, given the similarities in certain cultural experiences and social realities. 
 The filmmakers also expressed interest in exploring greater collaboration between Indian and Ghanaian filmmakers, including opportunities to bring creative talent, stories and cinematic experiences from Ghana to India and vice versa. Such partnerships, they observed, could foster cultural understanding, create new opportunities for filmmakers and strengthen the visibility of African cinema on international platforms. 
 The Press Conference was moderated by Shri. Manan Singh.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Beyond the Final Frame: The Magic of IFFI Evenings
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Beyond the Final Frame: The Magic of IFFI Evenings 
 Goa's Evenings Come Alive with Open-Air Screenings, Cultural Performances and Creative Exchanges 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:47PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 As the sun sets over the Mandovi River and the streets of Panaji light up, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) assumes a different rhythm. While the day is filled with film screenings, masterclasses, red-carpet appearances and conversations on cinema, the evenings bring their own charm. At IFFI, the setting sun does not signal the end of the festival day; it marks the beginning of another celebration. 
 Moving beyond the conventional confines of cinema halls, IFFI 2026 brings the cinematic experience closer to the public through open-air screenings at Miramar beach, Ravindra Bhavan in Margao and the helipad area at Vagator beach. Scheduled between 7 PM and 10 PM, these screenings feature a curated selection of films. Under the open skies of Goa, residents, visitors and cinema enthusiasts can come together to experience the joy of watching films, reflecting the festival’s commitment to making cinema more accessible and inclusive. 
 The festive atmosphere extends to the Mandovi promenade, where cultural performances of Romtamel bring Goa’s rich artistic traditions to the forefront. Scheduled across four evenings on November 23 rd to 27 th , the performances by seven cultural groups add a distinct local flavour to the international gathering. The coming together of indigenous cultural expressions and global cinematic traditions reflects the unique identity that Goa brings to IFFI. 
 Adding to the festivities, the IFFI Parade on 25 th November, themed ‘Celebrating the Joy of Cinema’, proceeds from the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) premises to Kala Academy in Panaji, featuring colourful floats, cultural performances and community participation. The parade extends the festival beyond its designated venues, enabling local residents and visitors to become part of the cinematic celebration. 
 For filmmakers, delegates and aspiring artists, however, the festival evenings offer more than entertainment. Beyond the scheduled screenings and formal interactions, they provide opportunities for informal conversations, creative exchanges and meaningful connections. A discussion about a film can lead to an exchange of cultural perspectives, while a chance encounter between filmmakers can lay the foundation for a future collaboration. 
 Behind the illuminated festival venues also lies the sustained effort of volunteers, technical crews, media professionals and organizers who work beyond screening hours to ensure the smooth conduct of the festival. Their contributions form an integral, often unseen, part of the IFFI experience. 
 The transformation of Panaji after sunset is itself a spectacle. Canopies of golden fairy lights adorn the city’s tree-lined avenues, while illuminated buildings, colourful installations and IFFI’s iconic peacock motifs lend a festive character to the streets. The city’s architecture and public spaces become an extension of the festival, reflecting how Goa’s association with IFFI has evolved into a distinctive celebration where the character of the host state complements the universal appeal of cinema. 
 In keeping with the theme of IFFI 2026, ‘Stories Without Borders’, the festival nights embody cinema’s ability to transcend not only geographical and linguistic boundaries but also the physical boundaries of the auditorium. They remind audiences that the magic of a film festival lies as much in the conversations it inspires and the connections it creates as in the stories unfolding on screen. 
 At IFFI, the credits may roll, the curtains may close and the lights inside the theatres may fade, but the celebration of cinema continues. In Goa, the festival clock simply refuses to stop.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: When Words Fall Short, Music Speaks: Singer K.S. Chithra Remembers the Voices of Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki at the 57th IFFI
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 When Words Fall Short, Music Speaks: Singer K.S. Chithra Remembers the Voices of Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki at the 57th IFFI 
 The Celebrated Singer Revisits the Voices and Songs that Shaped Generations and Her own Musical Journey through Cherished Memories and Heartfelt Anecdotes 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 Some voices do more than fill a room with music. They become part of our childhood, accompany us through life’s milestones and remain with us long after a song has ended. For celebrated singer K. S. Chithra, the voices of Asha Bhosle, S. Janaki and Lata Mangeshkar have been just that. At a masterclass titled “ Lata Mangeshkar Talk: The Voice That Echoes Forever in the Memory of Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki” at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Chithra took the audience on a deeply personal journey through the music and memories of the legendary singers, moderated by actor and filmmaker Suhasini Maniratnam. 
 The conversation began on a note of warmth and familiarity, with Chithra admitting that she was a little tense but confident that Suhasini would put her at ease. Their shared history soon found its way into the conversation, as Suhasini recalled how songs from films in which Chithra had lent her voice had become an integral part of her own journey. What followed was less a formal discussion and more a meeting of memories, with anecdotes often giving way to melodies. 
 Looking back at her beginnings, Chithra spoke of growing up in a family with a strong musical environment, participating in competitions and learning classical music. Singing, she said, was the one thing she knew she could do well, although she had never imagined it would take her so far. Her entry into film music seemed almost accidental. She recalled singing film songs at recreational clubs, often beginning with songs made popular by P. Susheela. 
 Asked about the voices she admired most, Chithra named P. Susheela, S. Janaki and Lata Mangeshkar. She even used to imitate Janaki in her childhood days, laughing as she admitted that the singer’s distinctive style was impossible to reproduce. Speaking of Lata Mangeshkar, Chithra reflected on the emotional depth of her singing, particularly her devotional songs, and shared one of her favourite Lata Mangeshkar melodies with the audience. 
 Her memories of Asha Bhosle revealed a different kind of admiration. Chithra spoke of Asha Bhosle’s extraordinary versatility and willingness to experiment across musical forms, including ghazals, one of which she herself hummed during the session. She recalled that Asha had always wanted to carve out her own musical identity rather than be compared with her sister Lata Mangeshkar. Chithra also shared a memorable first meeting, when Asha Bhosle asked her why she was singing in such a high range. It was a small exchange that offered a glimpse into the frankness and individuality of the legendary singer. 
 The memories of S. Janaki, however, carried a particularly affectionate note. Chithra recalled the early days of S. Janaki’s musical journey, when mimicry artists performed on stage and Janaki was often invited to sing in between their performances to fill the gaps. These opportunities gave audiences a chance to hear her voice, eventually leading her towards a career in playback singing. She also spoke of Janaki’s distinctive voice, expressive range and ability to bring life to every song. Beyond the music, Chithra remembered her as a mother figure. Recalling visits to Janaki’s home, she spoke fondly of how the veteran singer would lovingly feed her by hand, adding that even spicy food tasted sweet when it came from her. 
 Throughout the session, Suhasini brought songs into the conversation, connecting memories with the emotions they had carried on screen. She reflected on how film music accompanies people through love, weddings, grief and happiness, often expressing what words cannot. Chithra, in turn, revealed that the Malayalam song ‘Swarnamukile’ was one that could still bring her to tears. 
 A playful musical quiz added another dimension to the afternoon. Presented with film scenes without their background scores, Chithra identified and sang the songs from all five sequences, including songs from Suhasini’s films. The session also touched upon the demands of recording, difficult songs and the importance of recognising one’s vocal limitations with age. 
 The conversation reached its most memorable moment as Chithra began singing ‘Paadariyen’ from Sindhu Bhairavi. Suhasini joined her, lip-syncing to the song, as the two shared a moment that brought their conversation full circle. It was a beautiful meeting of music and memory, a reminder that songs are never just melodies, but pieces of lives, friendships and journeys that continue to resonate across generations.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Making Audiences Laugh Is a Serious Creative Exercise: Anil Ravipudi at IFFI 2026 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:47PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 “Making audiences laugh is a demanding creative exercise”, said National Film Award-winning filmmaker Shri Anil Ravipudi at a press conference on his film Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The 164-minute Telugu-language feature is among the five films selected for the Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama at IFFI 2026. The director was joined by producers Shri Sahu Garapati and Ms. K. Sushmita and actor Ms. Catherine Tresa. 
 “Comedy is always a serious business,” remarked Shri Ravipudi, explaining the challenges of writing humour while balancing family emotions and the expectations associated with a superstar like Chiranjeevi. He observed that it is difficult to predict which jokes will resonate with audiences. Crediting his writing team for its support, the director said his endeavour has been to craft stories that appeal to audiences across age groups. 
 Written and directed by Shri Ravipudi, Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu follows a national security officer whose devotion to his profession leaves him estranged from his wife and children. Six years later, he seeks to reconnect with them by taking up a position at their school. Blending humour and action with family emotions, the film explores the tension between professional duty and personal relationships, and the possibility of reconciliation. 
 Reflecting on his experience of directing Chiranjeevi, Shri Ravipudi recalled growing up watching the veteran actor’s films. His familiarity with the actor’s diverse roles over the years helped him develop a simple family narrative that showcased Chiranjeevi’s distinctive strengths. 
 Speaking about his association with the films being released around Sankranti, the director said the festive season naturally lends itself to family entertainers, as families come together and visit theatres. He observed that cinema offers audiences much-needed relief from the stresses of everyday life, adding that the joy of bringing smiles to their faces was a major motivation for him to continue making such films. 
 Ms. Catherine Tresa, who plays an important character in the film, described working alongside the veteran actor as a valuable learning experience. Speaking about her transition from serious roles to lighter ones, she emphasised the importance of versatility and understanding the director’s vision. She also expressed happiness at the film’s selection for IFFI, having wanted to connect with a wider audience through a commercial entertainer. 
 Welcoming the recognition of mainstream cinema at film festivals, Shri Ravipudi appreciated the jury’s efforts to accommodate different kinds of films. He observed that festivals could celebrate artistic and technical excellence while also recognising commercially successful films that connect with large audiences. 
 The film’s presentation at IFFI highlights the place of popular cinema alongside diverse cinematic traditions, celebrating stories that bring families together through humour, emotion and shared experiences. 
 The session was moderated by Swati Aggarwal.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 ‘Bhai Band’ Brings a Melodious Tale of Brotherhood, Tradition and Changing Times to IFFI 2026 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:17PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 Bhai Band , a Gujarati film directed by Manish Saini, featured in the Gala Premier section of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa today. The film follows two brothers who run a traditional wedding band in their village. Their lives take an unexpected turn when a disagreement drives them apart. When one brother returns weeks later with a DJ system and massive speakers, armed with nothing more than a playlist on his phone, the traditional band faces an unexpected challenge. What follows is a story that examines the impact of technological advancement on traditional occupations and the relationships that hold families together. 
 Addressing a press conference organised by PIB today, Director Manish Saini emphasised that although rooted in the Gujarati language and cultural setting, the film's underlying message and plot are universal and relatable to audiences across India. He also highlighted the importance of popularising artistic expressions and stories rooted in regional cinema, enabling them to reach wider audiences. Saini said that he was particularly fond of the film’s title, as it can be interpreted both as a reference to the camaraderie between two brothers and as a reference to a wedding band. 
 Actor Prit Kamani described Bhai Band as a unique film, filled with colours and enthusiasm. Marking his first Gujarati film, he spoke about his experience of working with Director Manish Saini and appreciated the ease and creative freedom he experienced during the filmmaking process. The actor also shared an amusing anecdote from the casting process, recalling how he had himself requested the director to conduct a screen test before finalising him for the role. 
 Actor Chirag Katrecha spoke about the process of understanding and internalising his character to bring authenticity to the performance. He also highlighted the challenges involved in portraying a singer, describing it as a demanding yet engaging experience. 
 Sharing insights into her character, actress Shraddha Dangar described her character as a lovely and cheerful personality. Reflecting on her experience, she spoke warmly about the collaboration and the enjoyable time spent working with the entire team. 
 Through humour, music and an engaging narrative, Bhai Band brings to the screen a story that goes beyond the changing sound of wedding celebrations. It raises questions about the intersection of technology, traditional livelihoods and human relationships, while celebrating the cultural vibrancy of regional storytelling. 
 The press interaction was moderated by Shri Kiran Murali.
