https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Baapya Explores Acceptance, Understanding and Relationships: Director Samir Tewari
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Baapya Explores Acceptance, Understanding and Relationships: Director Samir Tewari 
 Art Mirrors Society and Guides Social Progress: Actor Girish Kulkarni 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 2:45PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 Baapya , a Marathi comedy-drama set in coastal Maharashtra, explores gender identity, family relationships and social acceptance through an intimate story of personal choices and changing societal perceptions. The film is featured in the Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama at the 57th International Film Festival of India. Baapya Director cum Producer Samir Tewari and actor Girish Kulkarni interacted with the media at a press conference organised by PIB on the sidelines of the festival. 
 In his opening remarks, Samir Tewari emphasised that the film does not aim to preach or offer lessons to society, but simply tells a story about acceptance, understanding and relationships. "It's just a story about somebody wanting to become who they want to be, and people around them accepting them the way they are." he said. 
 Explaining his decision to make the film in Marathi, Tewari said he wanted to make an honest film rooted in a genuine script rather than one designed around an actor. 
 Recalling the challenges during production, Tewari said securing financial backing for the project was difficult, as potential investors considered its subject risky despite appreciating the script. Casting the lead character, Baapya, was another major challenge, as several actresses were hesitant about portraying a character whose gender identity differed from their own. He credited actress Rajashri Deshpande for taking up the role fearlessly and approaching it as a demanding creative challenge. 
 Reflecting on changing gender perceptions, Tewari said society is gradually moving towards blurring conventional distinctions between men and women. He observed that individual choices in clothing, behaviour and identity should not invite judgement or discrimination. " Within every man there is a woman and within every woman there is a man. The faster a society progresses, the more the lines will blur between gender," he remarked, emphasising the need to move beyond rigid social notions. 
 Actor Girish Kulkarni highlighted the importance of treating every individual with dignity and without prejudice. Drawing an analogy from nature, he said people accept the diversity of trees and plants without judging their forms, and the same spirit should guide human relationships. 
 Observing that art can play a significant role in shaping society, Kulkarni said cinema and other art forms serve not only as mirrors of contemporary realities but also as guides for social progress. He added that Baapya seeks to reinterpret traditions in the light of changing times without abandoning cultural roots. " We aren't forgetting our tradition; we are bringing it forward by interpreting it in a new way, and while strengthening our own roots, we are also thinking ahead. And then we have this immense love coming out of that process,” he pointed out. 
 Kulkarni further described acceptance and love as the film's underlying spirit, saying that embracing differences in language, clothing and identity reflects India's distinctive strength of unity in diversity. Referring to India's philosophical traditions, he said acceptance and the ability to look at the present without prejudice are deeply rooted in Indian thought. "I feel like I personally experienced that journey within myself, and that's how we were able to translate it onto celluloid," he said. 
 Highlighting the significance of IFFI as a platform for cultural and intellectual exchange, Kulkarni said the festival brings together filmmakers and audiences from India and abroad, creating opportunities to encounter diverse cinematic perspectives and engage in meaningful discussions. 
 The Press Conferenece was moderated by Supriya Ghaytadak.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Sixth Edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow Celebrates Emerging Filmmaking Talent at IFFI 2026
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Sixth Edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow Celebrates Emerging Filmmaking Talent at IFFI 2026 
 100 young creators from 13 filmmaking disciplines complete an intensive 48-hour filmmaking challenge Stay connected and continue working as a team; CMOT is just the beginning: IFFI Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 1:57PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 From developing a story to bringing it to the screen, 100 young creative professionals put their filmmaking skills to the test in an intensive 48-hour challenge as the sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT) concluded at the 57 th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. The initiative brought together emerging talent from across the country, culminating in the screening of films created by five teams and the presentation of awards across fifteen categories. 
 The concluding ceremony was attended by Festival Director of the 57 th IFFI and filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker; Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat; Managing Director of NFDC and Vice-Chancellor of FTII, Dhiraj Singh and members of jury. The Great Grand Jury was comprised of Aimee Baruah, Premraj, Madhu Apsara, Rumi Jaffrey, and Medha Kherdekar Reddy. 
 Winners of CMOT 2026 
 1. Best Film: One Last Stop, directed by Mohak Gandhi (Red Team), awarded ₹5 lakh. 
 2. Runner-up Film: A Little Something, directed by Tamanna Thakur (Green Team), awarded ₹3 lakh. 
 3. Best Director: Tamanna Thakur, A Little Something (Green Team). 
 4. Best Actor: Siddhi Parkar, Shells (Blue Team). 
 5. Best Cinematographer: Triasha Manna, One Last Stop (Red Team). 
 6. Best Editor: Nayan Chotaliya and Manav Agarwal, A Little Something (Green Team). 
 7. Best Scriptwriter: Jithin S, Shells (Blue Team). 
 8. Best Sound Design: Aswin Ashok, Two Sunsets and Zero Sunrises (Yellow Team). 
 9. Best Playback Singer: Sree Parvati S, Shells (Blue Team). 
 10. Best Music Composer: Akshay Anmol Katore, Neel Machli (Beige Team). 
 11. Best Costume Design: Srushti Wagh and Rupalika Paul, One Last Stop (Red Team). 
 12. Best Hair and Makeup Artist: Kashish Jaiswal, Shells (Blue Team). 
 13. Best Art Design: Srushti Wagh and Rupalika Paul, One Last Stop (Red Team). 
 14. Best Animation and VFX Artist: Harsh Sahani and Prakash Kumar Mehta, Neel Machli (Beige Team). 
 15. Best Voice-over/Dubbing: Sudeksha Sarkar, A Little Something (Green Team). 
 A bridge to the industry 
 Congratulating the participants on completing the 48-hour filmmaking challenge, Additional Secretary Prabhat described CMOT as a bridge between emerging talent and the film industry. He said the initiative provides young creators with an opportunity to demonstrate their abilities and connect with industry professionals. 
 Referring to this year’s theme, ‘ Roots & Wings: Honouring our Roots, Embracing our Futur e,’ he highlighted the coming together of cultural heritage, innovation and technology. He also pointed to the growing opportunities in the AVGC-XR sector, which is opening new avenues for young professionals in the creative industries. 
 Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker congratulated all the teams on their work and emphasised that filmmaking is inherently collaborative. He reminded the participants that a film is never the work of one individual, but the outcome of several creative disciplines coming together. Encouraging them to maintain the bonds formed during the challenge, he urged the young filmmakers to stay connected, continue working as teams and build on the experience, describing CMOT as just the beginning of their journey. 
 48 hours, five teams, one creative challenge 
 The filmmaking challenge began on 21 November, with the 100 participants divided into five teams of 20, identified by the colours Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, and Beige. Working under the common theme ‘Roots & Wings: Honouring our Roots, Embracing our Future,’ each team was tasked with conceptualising, shooting and completing a short film within 48 hours. 
 The challenge brought together participants from 13 filmmaking disciplines, including direction, acting, cinematography, editing, sound design, scriptwriting, art direction, animation, visual effects, music composition, playback singing, hair and makeup, and costume design. After shooting at locations across Goa, the teams moved to the dedicated post-production hub at Kala Academy, where they worked against the clock on editing, sound mixing and visual finishing to meet the deadline. 
 The resulting films reflected the participants’ creative interpretations of the theme, as well as their ability to collaborate across disciplines and deliver under demanding conditions. 
 Building pathways for emerging talent 
 Since its inception in 2021, CMOT has evolved into a platform connecting emerging creative professionals with the media and entertainment industry. Its alumni have gone on to work on international productions and received recognition at platforms and festivals including Cannes, the Berlinale, the Toronto International Film Festival and the International Emmy Awards. 
 In a notable outcome from the previous edition, 18 participants were selected by Mukesh Chhabra Casting Company (MCCC), demonstrating the initiative’s potential to translate emerging talent into professional opportunities. 
 The Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) curated and conducted the filmmaking challenge in collaboration with the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC). FTII faculty members mentored the participants throughout the process, while the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) facilitated shooting permissions at locations across the state.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Signs MoU with Directorate General of Training to Skill 1 Lakh Youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Jal Shakti 
 Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Signs MoU with Directorate General of Training to Skill 1 Lakh Youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 
 Ministry of Jal Shakti partners with Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship to strengthen the skilled workforce for sustainable rural water supply services Initiative to Create New Employment Opportunities for Rural Youth by Building a Skilled Local Workforce of ‘Nal Jal Mitras’ Programme to Roll Out Water Supply Operation and Maintenance Training Through ITIs and NSTIs Nationwide 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi 
 In a significant stride towards ensuring long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure and generating local employment, the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) , Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), and the Directorate General of Training (DGT) , Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 (JJM 2.0) . 
 The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri C. R. Patil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, Hon’ble Minister of State, Jal Shakti and Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, at the residence office of Hon’ble MoJS, New Delhi. 
 The agreement was formally executed by Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, NJJM and Shri Sunil Kumar Gupta , Deputy Director General, DGT. Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MoSDE, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, NJJM, and senior officials from both Ministries were present during the MoU signing. 
 The Hon’ble Union Ministers present on the occasion appreciated the initiative, highlighting its significance in strengthening rural water supply systems through a skilled local workforce and creating livelihood opportunities for rural youth. They acknowledged the importance of inter-ministerial collaboration under the ‘whole of government’ approach in leveraging the country’s vocational training infrastructure to support the objectives of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. 
 Briefing on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and the skilling initiative, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena , Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, said that with nearly 16 crore rural households now connected through tap water supply systems, the next priority is establishing a robust operation and maintenance ecosystem capable of supporting these assets over the long term. He stressed that timely technical support should be available within villages and nearby areas so that routine operational issues can be addressed quickly without dependence on external agencies. 
 Shri Meena highlighted that the partnership between DDWS and DGT would connect India's vocational training ecosystem directly with the rural water sector. Through structured classroom learning and hands-on exposure at functioning village water supply schemes, a new cadre of trained youth will be developed to support operations and maintenance activities. He added that the database of certified candidates would be made available at district and Gram Panchayat levels, enabling States and UTs to engage skilled personnel in accordance with their respective policies and requirements. 
 The MoU formalises a collaborative framework between DDWS and DGT for implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The initiative aims to create a trained and certified workforce capable of supporting the operation and maintenance of rural piped water supply systems while leveraging the existing ITI and NSTI network across the country. 
 Key Features of the Programme 
 Scale & Financial Outlay: The MoU targets the training and certification of at least 1,00,000 (one lakh) candidates during the extended period of the Jal Jeevan Mission, with an estimated outlay of approximately ₹111.93 crore borne entirely by DDWS from its departmental-level expenditure. 
 165-Hour NSQF-Aligned Course: Developed by the Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI) under DGT in consultation with DDWS and approved by NCVET , the short-term training (STT) course comprises 120 hours of institutional training (theory and practical) and 45 hours of mandatory On-the-Job Training (OJT) . 
 Target Group & Dual Certification: Offered as an optional elective for existing and pass-out trainees of Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) Fitter and Plumber trades across Government ITIs and NSTIs. On successful completion, trainees will receive an NSQF-aligned Short-Term Training (STT) certificate from DGT in addition to their National Trade Certificate (NTC) . 
 Hands-on Competencies & Field Exposure: The curriculum covers plumbing, water distribution systems, pumps and motors, basic electrical work, water quality monitoring, and routine O&M. Through the 45-hour OJT—facilitated by DDWS at functioning rural piped water supply schemes—trainees will gain direct experience in real-world village conditions. 
 Implementation & Governance: The National Instructional Media Institute (NIMI) , a subordinate office of DGT, will serve as the Training Partner for fund disbursement, training coordination, assessment, and certification. DDWS will support trainer orientation, OJT site identification, and share the database of certified candidates at District and Gram Panchayat levels for potential engagement in O&M roles in accordance with respective State HR policies. A Joint Steering Committee , chaired by an officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary, DDWS, will oversee rollout, targets, and fund utilisation.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: India's MSME Growth Story Hits a New High: 10 Crore Registrations, 10 Crore Steps for a Vibrant and Strong Aatmanirbhar Bharat!
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises 
 India's MSME Growth Story Hits a New High: 10 Crore Registrations, 10 Crore Steps for a Vibrant and Strong Aatmanirbhar Bharat! 
 Transforming MSME Registration; from paper work to a seamless digital ecosystem 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi 
 India's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector has achieved a milestone, crossing 10 crore registrations on the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform on 30 October 2026 . This achievement marks a defining moment in India's journey towards building a more formalised, inclusive and digitally empowered MSME sector. 
 A Landmark Achievement in MSME Formalisation. 
 The combined strength of the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform has taken India's MSME formalisation journey to a new level. The growth from 1.02 crore registrations in 2020 to over 10 crore in 2026 demonstrates the increasing adoption of digital platforms and the Government's sustained commitment to bringing enterprises into the formal economic framework. 
 The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises launched the Udyam Registration Portal on 1 July 2020 , providing enterprises with a simple, transparent, online and paperless platform for registration. This digital initiative has significantly streamlined registration procedures, enhanced ease of doing business and enabled enterprises to become part of India's formal economic ecosystem. 
 Evolution of MSME Registration in India: From EM-II to Udyam Registration 
 India's MSME registration framework has evolved significantly over the years, moving from a largely physical and document-intensive process to a technology-driven, entrepreneur-friendly digital ecosystem. 
 Key milestones in this journey: 
 1. Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM-II) – 2006 to 17 September 2015 
 MSME registration was primarily a physical process, requiring entrepreneurs to submit applications along with the requisite documents for verification by the District Industries Centre (DIC). During this nine-year period, 21.96 lakh MSMEs were registered. 
 2. Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) – 18 September 2015 to 30 June 2020 
 A significant shift towards digital registration took place with the introduction of the Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM). Based on Aadhaar, the online system simplified the earlier registration procedure and reduced the compliance burden on entrepreneurs. Around 1.02 crore MSMEs registered during this five-year period. 
 3. Udyam Registration – From 1 July 2020 
 A major digital transformation was ushered in with the launch of the Udyam Registration Portal. The registration process became fully online, paperless and based on self-declaration, eliminating the requirement for physical documents or proof uploads. 
 Integration with Aadhaar and PAN-based details, along with GST and Income Tax databases, further streamlined the registration process. The system also eliminated the requirement for renewal and made registration completely free of cost, making formalisation simpler and more accessible for entrepreneurs across the country. 
 4. Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) – From 11 January 2023 
 Recognising that a large number of micro-enterprises, particularly those operating in the informal sector, faced difficulties in accessing registration facilities, the Ministry introduced the Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) on 11 January 2023. 
 The platform facilitates the formalisation of eligible informal micro-enterprises through a simplified mechanism involving designated financial institutions and other partner agencies. 
 Udyam: Enabling Access, Recognition and Inclusive Growth 
 Udyam registration supports the identification of enterprises by banks and financial institutions, facilitating the implementation of initiatives such as the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), Priority Sector Lending and other credit and Finance related programmes. 
 It strengthens the foundation for inclusive economic development by bringing women entrepreneurs, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs, rural enterprises, traditional artisans and other disadvantaged sections into the formal economic framework. 
 Furthermore, formal recognition through Udyam supports the broader objectives of various Government initiatives, including the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), National SC-ST Hub, Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises and other entrepreneurship development programmes, subject to applicable eligibility requirements. 
 Driving Inclusive Growth: Participation of Women 
 The registration data of both Udyam and Udyam Assist reflects the following: 
 Women-led MSMEs: 3.76 crore registrations, accounting for 37.8% . 
 These figures underline the role of digital registration in expanding formal recognition among diverse sections of society and strengthening the foundation of inclusive entrepreneurship. 
 The milestone of 10 crore registrations is not merely a number; it represents millions of enterprises taking steps towards formal recognition and becoming part of India's growth story. It reflects the growing confidence of entrepreneurs in India's digital ecosystem and the collective momentum towards a stronger, more inclusive and self-reliant economy. 
 *** 
 PC/KG

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: First Regional Workshop on Implementation of Sixteenth Finance Commission Recommendations for Rural Local Body Grants to be held in Goa tomorrow
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj 
 First Regional Workshop on Implementation of Sixteenth Finance Commission Recommendations for Rural Local Body Grants to be held in Goa tomorrow 
 Western Region States to chart a roadmap for timely and effective utilisation of 16th Finance Commission grants and augmentation of Own Sources of Revenue 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:51PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Panaji /New Delhi : 25 November 2026 
 The Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR), Government of India, will organize the first Regional Workshop on implementation of the Sixteenth Finance Commission (XVI FC) Recommendations for Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) grants in Goa tomorrow, 26 November 2026. Smt. Mukta Shekhar, Joint Secretary, MoPR, will be joined by senior officers from the participating States of Goa, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. The Workshop seeks to build a shared understanding of the 16th Finance Commission’s recommendations, the Operational Guidelines and the compliance conditions among the Western Region States, so that the 16th Finance Commission grants reach Panchayats on time and translate into visible improvements in the lives of rural citizens. 
 The Sixteenth Finance Commission has recommended grants of ₹4,35,236 crore to PRIs (Panchayati Raj Institutions) / RLBs (Rural Local Bodies) across all 28 States for the award period 2026-27 to 2030-31. The Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, issued the Operational Guidelines for their implementation on 21 May 2026. The Commission has also recommended that MoPR extend guidance and handholding support to States and organise Regional Workshops to familiarise them with various aspects of the recommendations. The Goa Workshop is the first in this series. 
 The Workshop builds on the National Workshop of State Panchayati Raj Ministers held by MoPR on 3 July 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, to discuss implementation of the 16th FC recommendations for PRIs/ RLBs. While the National Workshop set the policy direction, the Regional Workshops carry the dialogue closer to the officers responsible for delivery on the ground. 
 Reflecting the Ministry’s continuing efforts and focus on augmentation of Own Sources of Revenue (OSR), the Workshop also seeks to deliberate on experiences and best practices that enhance the fiscal self-reliance of Panchayats. Elected Representatives and officers from the host State, Goa, are also expected to participate. 
 Financially empowered, capable and accountable Panchayats are central to the vision of Atmanirbhar Panchayat and Viksit Panchayat, which pave the way for Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. Timely devolution of Finance Commission grants, together with steadily growing OSR, will enable Panchayats to plan, deliver and serve their communities with greater confidence. The Workshop is being hosted with the support of the Department of Panchayati Raj, Government of Goa, and the Ministry looks forward to a productive and collaborative exchange among all participating States.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Constitution Day, 2026 to be observed on 26th November
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs 
 Constitution Day, 2026 to be observed on 26th November 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) will be observed on 26 th November, 2026, to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26 th November, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015, under kind guidance of the Prime Minister of India. 
 As part of the celebrations, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. This initiative will provide an opportunity to citizens across the country to read the Preamble and reaffirm their commitment to the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution. 
 Members of the public, Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, State/UT Governments, educational institutions, schools, colleges, universities and other organisations are encouraged to participate in the initiative through the following platform: 
 MyGov: https://pledge.mygov.in/constitution-day-2026/ , read the Preamble, get a certificate and share it on social media. 
 Constitution Quiz through the MyGov and MyBharat portals from 18 th to 26 th November, 2026 and Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad is being organised across 786 districts in all 36 States/Union Territories from 24 th to 26 th November, 2026, to encourage participation and engagement of youth. 
 Various activities are being organised across the country by Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, State/UT Governments and their respective field formations, attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and institutions to mark the occasion. These activities include collective reading of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks, runs and other community engagement activities. 
 Educational institutions are also being encouraged to organise special morning assemblies, discussions and competitions to familiarise students with the making of the Constitution, its salient features. 
 Special emphasis is being laid on extending the celebrations to the grassroots level through active participation of citizens, young people and students. Various awareness and outreach activities are also being undertaken through digital platforms and community-based initiatives to promote understanding of the Constitution and its significance in the country's democratic framework. 
 Constitution Day provides an occasion to reflect upon the principles and values enshrined in the Constitution of India and to renew our collective commitment to its ideals. The observance seeks to strengthen constitutional awareness, promote responsible citizenship and encourage active participation in upholding the democratic values of the nation. 
 Citizens, particularly young people and students are encouraged to participate enthusiastically in the Constitution Day activities and join in reaffirming their commitment to the Constitution of India. 
 ***

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: NHAI to Ensure Availability of Incident Management Services Before Opening of National Highway Stretches
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
 NHAI to Ensure Availability of Incident Management Services Before Opening of National Highway Stretches 
 New guidelines strengthen emergency response mechanism through availability of ambulances, patrol vehicles and tow-away cranes 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi 
 In order to strengthen emergency services on National Highways, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued guidelines to ensure availability of Incident Management Services (IMS) on National Highways before opening of stretch to traffic. The objective is to strengthen road safety and ensure timely assistance to National Highway users during accidents, vehicle breakdowns and other emergencies. 
 Incident Management Services include availability of ambulances, route patrolling vehicles and tow-away cranes on National Highways. These services are supported by the integration of on-location teams with NHAI’s 1033 National Highway Helpline and coordination with local police, fire services and hospitals. 
 Ensuring IMS availability across National Highway network 
 The guidelines prescribe arrangements for ensuring availability of these services on different categories of National Highway stretches. On operational National Highway stretches, ambulances are positioned at the user fee plazas or other suitable locations, based on accident data and requirement of the stretch. 
 For National Highways entrusted to NHAI by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, ambulances will be deployed through a centralised agency in accordance with the delegated powers of NHAI field offices. Route patrolling vehicles and tow-away cranes will be arranged through separate tenders or as part of highway maintenance and strengthening works. 
 Apart from this, on National Highway stretches that have not been entrusted to NHAI but are tolled by NHAI, deployment of IMS will follow the procedure laid down by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. Under this, ambulances will be deployed through NHAI’s centralised agency in coordination with the concerned Regional Office of the Ministry/NHIDCL, while route patrolling vehicles and tow-away cranes on such stretches will be arranged by the concerned authority. 
 With this initiative, NHAI aims to provide National Highway users with timely assistance and enhance overall safety on the National Highway network across the country. 
 *** 
 GDH/DS/HJ

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Smt. Annapurna Devi Launch Nayi Chetna 5.0
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Rural Development 
 Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Smt. Annapurna Devi Launch Nayi Chetna 5.0 
 15 Ministries/Departments Join Hands for Women’s Safety, Gender Equality and Empowerment Landmark MoU Signed to Make Villages Violence-Free Month-Long Nationwide Campaign to Be Conducted Across All States and UTs from 25 November to 23 December 2026 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:48PM by PIB Delhi 
 Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and Smt. Annapurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development, today launched the fifth edition of “Nayi Chetna: Pahal Badlaav Ki”, the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment, at NASC Complex, PUSA, New Delhi. Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development; Shri Anil Malik, Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development; and Shri Niraj Verma, Secretary, Department of Justice, were present, along with senior officials of participating Ministries, State Governments, development partners and women leaders from across the country. 
 The centrepiece of the event was a landmark Quadripartite MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative (VFVI), signed by the Department of Rural Development, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The MoU links DAY-NRLM’s Gender Resource Centres with One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181, Disha 2.0 and legal aid services into a single chain of support, from prevention and protection to legal assistance and rehabilitation. To be piloted in 9 States and Union Territories, it rests on a simple promise: no woman facing violence should be left to find her way to help alone. 
 Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages. 
 Smt. Annapurna Devi highlighted the role of community institutions in taking the campaign to every household. Calling for wider use of support services, she urged citizens to remember, save and share Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Number 112, so that no woman in distress goes without timely help. 
 Shri Rohit Kansal traced Nayi Chetna’s journey from an awareness campaign to a nationwide, community-led movement, with 5.3 crore participants and nearly 7,000 Gender Resource Centres established so far. The fifth edition, he said, will turn that awareness and community trust into effective support, legal assistance and timely access to justice. 
 Shri Anil Malik called for seamless convergence of helplines, legal services and support institutions, backed by timely response and consistent follow-up. Highlighting the 16-day action agenda, he underlined the collective responsibility of families, communities and institutions towards women’s safety. 
 Shri Niraj Verma stressed the need to turn existing legal safeguards into services women can actually reach, particularly in rural and remote areas. He highlighted the role of NALSA, Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, paralegal volunteers and Gender Resource Centres in strengthening legal awareness, referrals and free legal aid. 
 An Inter-Ministerial Joint Advisory was also unveiled, extending the Whole-of-Government approach to address gender-based discrimination and violence and advance women’s economic empowerment. The collaborating Ministries/Departments are: Rural Development, Women and Child Development; School Education and Literacy; Home Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Social Justice and Empowerment; Youth Affairs and Sports; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises; Information and Broadcasting; Justice; Labour and Employment; Revenue; and Road Transport and Highways. 
 Led by DAY-NRLM, the campaign will run across all States and Union Territories until 23 December 2026, built around four themes: Identity, Assetization, Mobility, and Redistribution of Unpaid Care Work. Through Self-Help Groups and community institutions, it will reach rural India with awareness drives, rallies, community meetings, street plays and dialogues with men and youth. 
 The event also saw the release of the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report and the Nayi Chetna Anthem, and Gender Champions and One Stop Centre administrators shared experiences from the field. SHG women, Anganwadi workers, State Rural Livelihoods Missions and civil society partners took part in large numbers, reaffirming Nayi Chetna as a true Jan Andolan for gender equality. 
 ***

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Cheaper, Safer and Faster Credit for Rural Women: Department of Rural Development and NABARD Join Hands
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Rural Development 
 Cheaper, Safer and Faster Credit for Rural Women: Department of Rural Development and NABARD Join Hands 
 NABARD to be the single nodal agency for the Interest Subvention Scheme for women SHGs and the Women Enterprise Acceleration Fund; Interest Subvention Portal launched 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Department of Rural Development (DoRD) and the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) today signed an Agreement for Management and Technical Support for the Interest Subvention Scheme for women Self Help Groups and the Women Enterprise Acceleration Fund (WEAF) under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The Agreement was signed by Shri Vipin Kumar, Additional Secretary, DoRD, and Shri Ajay Kumar Sood, Deputy Managing Director, NABARD in the presence of Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Rural Development; Dr. Shaji Krishnan V, Chairman, NABARD. Following the signing, the Secretary and the Chairman jointly launched the Interest Subvention Portal. 
 Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Rural Development, said that the SHG movement, having achieved remarkable outreach and scale, is now entering a new phase focused on enterprise development. Over Rs. 14 lakh crore has already been mobilised as formal credit for SHGs, steadily replacing informal sources of credit in rural areas. Over the next five years, the Department aims to facilitate an additional Rs. 10 lakh crore for SHGs and Rs. 1 lakh crore for individual enterprises. 
 “Interest subvention will make credit more affordable, reimbursement of guarantee fees will make collateral-free credit safer, and the new portal will make the process faster,” the Secretary said. He called upon DoRD and NABARD to work closely to design customised credit products for SHG members, strengthen enterprise support systems, bridge information gaps on schemes, and build capacities for a robust and sustainable SHG ecosystem. 
 Under the Agreement, NABARD will serve as the single nodal agency for both schemes, covering Public Sector, Private Sector, Small Finance, Regional Rural and Cooperative Banks, and will provide technical, managerial and implementation support to the Department. Banks will now work with one set of rules, one reconciliation process and one point of accountability. 
 “This partnership combines NABARD’s institutional strengths with DAY-NRLM’s community network to accelerate the transition of SHG women from livelihoods to viable enterprises,” said Dr. Shaji Krishnan V, Chairman, NABARD. He reaffirmed NABARD’s commitment to deepening its collaboration with the Department to advance financial inclusion and women-led development. 
 Shri Vipin Kumar, Additional Secretary, Rural Development, said that women SHGs have earned a trusted place in the formal banking system through their financial discipline and creditworthiness. “The question before us is no longer whether banks should lend to rural women, but how quickly, how cheaply and how far that credit can take them,” he remarked. He added that with every participating bank onboarded on the portal, claims would be processed and settled on time. 
 The Agreement will strengthen the way credit support reaches rural women. Predictable and prompt reimbursement will give banks greater confidence to extend larger loans to women’s collectives, while lower costs and shared risk will open the door to enterprise finance for women. Over time, the portal’s real-time data will offer a clear view of how credit flows to rural women, enabling sharper targeting and better-informed policy under DAY-NRLM. Together, these measures mark a decisive step in turning Lakhpati Didis into rural entrepreneurs and employers. 
 Signing of the Agreement between DoRD and NABARD, and launch of the Interest Subvention Portal, New Delhi, 25 November 2026 
 *** 
 PU

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Addresses HealthX Elevate 2026, Highlights India’s Growing Healthcare Innovation Ecosystem
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Science & Technology 
 Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Addresses HealthX Elevate 2026, Highlights India’s Growing Healthcare Innovation Ecosystem 
 India’s Start-up Ecosystem Expands from Around 350 in 2014 to Over 2.5 Lakh, with More Than 60% from Tier-II and Tier-III Cities: Dr. Jitendra Singh AI, Genomics and Precision Medicine to Strengthen Early Diagnosis and Individualised Healthcare: Dr. Jitendra Singh India Needs Greater Industry Participation to Translate Healthcare Research into Globally Recognised Innovations: Dr. Jitendra Singh 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi 
 Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today highlighted India’s expanding StartUp ecosystem, growing capabilities in biotechnology and healthcare innovation, and the increasing role of artificial intelligence (AI), genomics and precision medicine in transforming healthcare, while addressing HealthX Elevate 2026. 
 The Minister noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest start-up ecosystem, with more than 60 per cent of StartUps coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities and smaller towns. 
 The event, themed around healthcare start-ups and innovation, brought together healthcare leaders, entrepreneurs, investors and experts to discuss the evolving landscape of healthcare innovation in India. 
 Speaking during a Fire Chat session, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India’s start-up ecosystem has undergone a remarkable transformation, expanding from around 350 start-ups in 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh today. He noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest start-up ecosystem, with more than 60 per cent of start-ups coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities. 
 The Minister said that the growth of start-ups is no longer confined to major metropolitan hubs such as Bengaluru, Delhi and Mumbai. Digital access and an enabling ecosystem have made information, resources and opportunities available to aspiring entrepreneurs across the country, allowing talent from smaller cities and towns to participate in the start-up movement. 
 Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the emergence of entrepreneurship beyond conventional technology and science-led fields. Referring to the growth of agri-based start-ups, he said that entrepreneurial success does not necessarily require a highly advanced academic qualification, but calls for passion, focus and the ability to use technology effectively. He added that the Government is extending technological and financial support to encourage entrepreneurship. 
 The Minister highlighted the significant expansion of India’s biotechnology start-up ecosystem, which, he said, has grown from around 50–60 start-ups in 2014 to nearly 10,000 today. He said that India is increasingly developing solutions not only for diseases prevalent in tropical regions, but also for conditions that were earlier primarily associated with other parts of the world. 
 Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India’s progress in vaccines has transformed the way the country’s healthcare capabilities are viewed globally. He referred to the development of the country’s DNA vaccine for COVID-19 and its supply to around 30 countries. He also highlighted advances in genetic and therapeutic research, including a successful trial of a genetic therapy for haemophilia, the findings of which were published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 
 Referring to developments in nuclear medicine, the Minister said that Indian researchers are working on cost-effective solutions for diseases, including acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. He noted that India is moving beyond addressing diseases traditionally associated with the country and is developing affordable therapeutic and diagnostic solutions with wider global relevance. 
 Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need for greater private-sector participation in biotechnology, healthcare research and innovation. He said that the Government is encouraging private partners to contribute to research and development, and expressed hope that India would produce a globally recognised blockbuster drug in the coming decade. 
 The Minister also highlighted India’s unique advantage in healthcare research due to its diverse population and genetic resources. He said that a comprehensive understanding of genetic data could help researchers generate insights relevant not only to India but also to the global scientific community. 
 On the role of artificial intelligence in healthcare, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that AI should be viewed as an enabling tool across disciplines rather than as a separate domain. He highlighted its potential in diagnosis, data collection and analysis, noting that processes which earlier took hours or days could now be completed in minutes with AI support. 
 Referring to the Genome India initiative, the Minister said that AI is facilitating the analysis of genetic information and supporting the study of diverse population groups. He noted that the Government had completed gene sequencing of 10,000 individuals, with the data covering 80 different population groups. 
 The Minister said that India is entering an era of individualised and precision medicine, in which treatment may be tailored to the genetic profile, lifestyle, environment and molecular characteristics of each patient. He noted that advances in research could enable doctors to move towards more personalised prescriptions, even for patients presenting with similar disease or investigation profiles. 
 He also underscored the growing importance of preventive healthcare, early detection and research into biomarkers that may help identify the likelihood of diseases before they develop. Referring to research on diabetes-related pregnancy, he said that scientists are working on biomarkers that could help assess the risk of diabetes in women at the time of delivery, enabling more targeted follow-up and preventive care.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: First North-East India-Specific antivenom developed against neglected Pit Vipers species
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Science & Technology 
 First North-East India-Specific antivenom developed against neglected Pit Vipers species 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi 
 A novel antivenom specifically effective against the venom of two particular pit vipers common in the North Eastern states can help improve treatment for snake bites common in these areas. and Meghalaya states in order to close this gap in snakebite treatment. 
 Northeast India is home to a wide variety of venomous snakes, making snakebite a major public health concern. However, India's "Big Four" snakes—Russell's viper, spectacled cobra, common krait, and saw-scaled viper—are the main targets of commercially marketed antivenom. The effectiveness of this polyvalent antivenom against a number of medically significant venomous snakes in Northeast India has been shown to be limited. 
 Snake bites from pit vipers—the Pope's pit viper ( Trimeresurus popeiorum ) and the red-tailed bamboo pit viper ( Trimeresurus erythrurus ) found in the North Eastern states are a common medical emergency in these areas. Snakebite is regarded as a neglected tropical disease and a medical emergency by the World Health Organization (WHO). The absence of antivenoms that can effective against venoms of these specific snakes leads to the the antivenom crisis in Northeast India, according to a recent study. 
 Fig: A schematic diagram depicting the superior neutralizing activity of Bi-AV compared to Indian PAV against pit vipers from North-east India. 
 A research team led by Prof. Ashis K. Mukherjee, Director of the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology (IASST), Guwahati, an Autonomous Institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) has created a novel equine F(ab)2 bivalent antivenom that is specifically effective against the venom of T. erythrurus and T. popeiorum that were collected from Mizoram and Meghalaya states in order to close this gap in snakebite treatment. 
 Researchers from IASST, Guwahati, Premium Serums and Vaccines Pvt. Ltd., Pune, Amrita Research Center Delhi-NCR, Mizoram University, and Aaranyak, Guwahati, collaborated on the project to demonstrate academic-industry cooperation. 
 In laboratory and preclinical investigations, the novel bivalent antivenom showed noticeably superior protection against pit viper envenomation of the NE region as compared to Indian polyvalent antivenom (Figure 1). Pit viper envenomation is characterized by disruptions in blood coagulation and injury to local and organ tissue, both of which are significantly reduced by the novel antivenom. 
 Prof. Mukherjee, who led the research stated that additional clinical and regulatory testing will be necessary before this novel antivenom is routinely used on patients and he is hopeful about it. The study published in the International Journal of Biological Macromolecules emphasizes the significance of creating region-specific antivenoms based on the snakes that cause severe envenomation in various regions of India, especially in Northeast India, where a number of medically significant species do not fit into the conventional "Big Four" paradigm. 
 Publication Link: 10.1016/j.ijbiomac.2026.154578

 Biotechnology Startups Grow from 50-60 in 2014 to Nearly 11,000; Bio-Economy Expands from 10 billion Dollars to 195 billion Dollars: Dr. Jitendra Singh Genomics and Multi-Omics Emerging as Strategic Technologies for Healthcare, Agriculture and Economic Growth: Dr. Jitendra Singh at CII Global Genomics Summit 2026 India’s Genetic Diversity Offers a Unique Global Advantage for Research and Innovation, says Dr. Jitendra Singh Industry Participation, Private Investment and R&D Partnerships Crucial to Translating Scientific Discoveries into Economic Opportunities, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

 India’s bio-economy is set to reach 300 billion Dollars by 2030, with biotechnology set to drive the next Industrial Revolution, while Biotech Startups in India had already grown from just 50-60 in 2014 to over 11,000 today, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said today, urging industry leaders, Startups and investors to seize emerging opportunities through greater investment and participation in genomics, multi-omics and advanced biotechnology. 
 Drawing a parallel with the transformative role of Information Technology in the previous industrial revolution, the Minister said that biotechnology is now emerging as a strategic technology platform that will shape the future of healthcare, agriculture and global economic competitiveness. He cautioned that businesses must adapt to the rapidly changing technological landscape, as those failing to embrace emerging technologies risk becoming irrelevant.

The same disease could require different treatment approaches for different individuals, making genomics an increasingly essential component of future medical practice. He said these technologies were no longer confined to research laboratories but were becoming indispensable for healthcare systems, businesses and nations seeking to remain competitive. 
 Emphasising India's unique advantage in genomic research, the Minister said the country's extraordinary genetic diversity could become a major global asset for research and development. India's diverse population groups and wide spectrum of diseases provide an extensive knowledge base for generating genomic data and developing solutions relevant to populations across the world. He said greater investment in genomic research would not only strengthen India's scientific capabilities but also create significant industrial and commercial opportunities. 
 Referring to the Genome India Project, he said whole-genome sequencing of 10,000 individuals representing 80 different population groups had already been undertaken, creating a valuable foundation for future research. He encouraged industry stakeholders to partner with government initiatives and translate this scientific resource into practical applications. 
 The Minister also drew attention to the extensive opportunities biotechnology offers in agriculture and livestock, beyond healthcare. Genomics and advanced biotechnology can help improve crop productivity, nutritional quality and resistance to pests and diseases, while supporting climate-resilient agriculture. He said the breadth of these applications offered businesses opportunities to specialise in different sectors and build sustainable, innovation-driven enterprises.

The establishment of bio-foundries and other enabling infrastructure is aimed at supporting research, startups and industry in translating scientific discoveries into commercially viable products.

He said these achievements demonstrated that India had reached a stage where its biotechnology innovations could find wider global markets and attract greater industry participation.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 
 Only Five Days Left to Apply for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Encourages Eligible Students to Avail Opportunity for Quality Residential Education 
 SHRESHTA Scheme Opens Doors to Quality Education in Reputed Private Residential Schools for Meritorious Scheduled Caste (SC) and Eligible De-notified Tribe (DNT) Students Eligible Students and Parents Encouraged to Complete Online Registration by November 30, 2026 National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) Scheduled to be Held on January 10, 2027 Candidates Can Apply Online at https://exams.nta.nic.in/shreshta 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi 
 With only five days remaining for the closure of online registration for the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, has called upon eligible students across the country to come forward and avail themselves of the opportunity to pursue quality education in reputed private residential schools under the SHRESHTA Scheme. 
 The Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA), implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, aims to provide quality education to meritorious students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and De-notified Tribes (DNTs) not covered under the SC, ST and OBC categories, thereby creating greater opportunities for academic advancement, social mobility and holistic development. 
 A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Scheme seeks to bridge educational disparities by enabling meritorious students from targeted communities to access conducive learning environments, pursue academic excellence and realise their full potential. Access to quality school education plays a pivotal role in strengthening academic capabilities and creating opportunities for a brighter and more secure future, the Official said. 
 With the registration deadline fast approaching, eligible students and their parents have been asked to complete the application process at the earliest and avoid last-minute difficulties, the Official said. 
 Wider awareness and dissemination of information about the Scheme, particularly in rural, remote and underserved areas, can help ensure that deserving students do not miss this important educational opportunity due to a lack of awareness, he said. 
 The Official said the online registration process for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027, being conducted in collaboration with the National Testing Agency (NTA), commenced on November 14, 2026, will remain open until November 30, 2026 (up to 11:50 PM). 
 The Official said to facilitate candidates in making necessary corrections to their submitted application forms, a correction window will remain operational from December 2 to December 4, 2026. 
 The National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027 is scheduled to be conducted on January 10, 2027 , he said. 
 Eligible candidates may submit their online applications through the official National Testing Agency (NTA) portal at https://exams.nta.nic.in/shreshta . 
 Candidates and their parents have been advised to carefully read the eligibility criteria and application-related instructions available on the official portal before completing the registration process. 
 Teachers, educational institutions, community organisations and other stakeholders have been urged to disseminate information about the Scheme among eligible students and their families to facilitate wider participation and ensure that the benefits of the initiative reach the intended beneficiaries across the country. 
 Through targeted educational interventions such as SHRESHTA, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to reaffirm its commitment to promoting equal educational opportunities, empowering future generations and ensuring that socio-economic disadvantages do not become barriers to educational advancement, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Shri B L Verma Launches ‘SAMAVESH’ and New e-Anudaan Portal to Strengthen Digital Governance and Inclusive Welfare Delivery
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 
 Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Shri B L Verma Launches ‘SAMAVESH’ and New e-Anudaan Portal to Strengthen Digital Governance and Inclusive Welfare Delivery 
 SAMAVESH Provides Unified Digital Access to Department’s Schemes, Services and Organisational Portals, Strengthening Citizen-Centric Governance AI-Powered ‘Samajik Sahayak’ Chatbot to Facilitate Access to Welfare Scheme Information in 22 Indian Languages through BHASHINI New e-Anudaan Portal to Simplify Grant-in-Aid Processes, Promote Ease of Doing Business and Strengthen Transparency and Accountability MoUs with BHASHINI and National Skill Development Corporation to Strengthen Multilingual Service Delivery, Skill Development and Employment Opportunities 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi 
 In a significant step towards strengthening technology-enabled governance and ensuring accessible, transparent and efficient delivery of social welfare services, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, launched SAMAVESH (Single Access Mechanism for All Verticals of Empowerment & Social Harmony) and the new e-Anudaan Portal, at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, in the National Capital here today. 
 The launch of SAMAVESH and the new e-Anudaan Portal marks a significant milestone in the Department’s digital transformation journey. These initiatives seek to make social welfare schemes and services more accessible, reduce procedural difficulties for beneficiaries and implementing organisations, and strengthen transparency, accountability and technology-enabled delivery of social welfare programmes. 
 Senior officers of the Ministry, representatives of NeGD, NIC, NGOs and other stakeholder organisations were also present on the occasion. 
 Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar described the launching of SAMAVESH and new e-Anudaan portals as historical and a game changer and highlighted the Department’s commitment towards leveraging technology to strengthen the delivery of welfare schemes and services. 
 The Minister emphasised that SAMAVESH represents an important step towards integrated, transparent and citizen-centric governance by bringing the Department’s digital services onto a common platform. 
 Dr Kumar also underscored the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital integration and data-driven monitoring in improving the accessibility, transparency and effectiveness of welfare delivery. 
 Speaking on the occasion, Shri B. L. Verma highlighted the importance of making Government schemes more accessible to beneficiaries through simplified digital services. He emphasised that technology-driven initiatives such as SAMAVESH would enable citizens, particularly those belonging to disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society, to access information and services more conveniently while promoting transparency and inclusion. 
 Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, described the launch as a golden day in the Ministry’s history, marking a significant leap in digital governance with the integration of 33 different portals into a single SAMAVESH Portal. 
 He highlighted that e-Anudaan 2.0 has reduced the number of forms from 283 to 182 , significantly easing procedural requirements for NGOs and institutions. The introduction of real-time remote inspections through Bharat VC with 15 minutes’ prior notice will further strengthen institutional monitoring and accountability. He also underscored the integration of AI, BHASHINI, DigiLocker and PFMS to enhance accessibility and efficiency. 
 Appreciating the efforts of the IT team under the leadership of Additional Secretary Ms. Mona K. Khandhar and Director Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, along with NeGD and NIC, the Secretary reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to advancing the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of Ease of Living through technology-enabled governance. 
 Developed by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), SAMAVESH provides a unified digital gateway to the Department’s schemes, services and organisational portals through https://www.dosje.gov.in/samavesh-citizen-portals/ ,enabling citizens to access a wide range of welfare-related information and services through a common platform. 
 The platform brings together six major scheme-related portals, including Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW), National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), SAMBAL - National Helpline Against Atrocities (NHAA), Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) and Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE) , covering welfare initiatives for transgender persons, rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging and Garima Greh. 
 SAMAVESH also brings together 12 organisational and institutional portals, including those of Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation, National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC) and the Department’s Social Justice Portal. 
 The unified platform is designed to simplify access to welfare schemes and services, eliminating the need for citizens to search across multiple websites. A common login facility provides a more consistent user experience, while a consolidated Beneficiary Dashboard is intended to facilitate access to beneficiary-related information and strengthen monitoring

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 
 From Financial Hardship To Academic Aspirations 
 NFSC Fellowship Supports A Research Scholar 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi 
 The journey of 28 year Deepak Kanojia (name changed) , highlights how financial support can complement perseverance and academic commitment, helping create opportunities for higher education and a more inclusive future. 
 Deepak Kanojia, a Scheduled Caste research scholar, is pursuing higher education with determination and the aspiration to build a better future. Coming from a financially constrained family, his academic journey has been marked by perseverance, resilience and a strong commitment to education. 
 As the first among four children in his family to pursue higher education, he faced considerable challenges in meeting tuition fees, accommodation costs, study materials and other essential expenses. 
 Limited family income and financial uncertainties often made continuing his studies difficult, and at several stages he faced the possibility of discontinuing his education. However, determined to advance his education and work towards self-reliance, he remained steadfast in his pursuit of higher studies. 
 The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme provided crucial support to Mr. Kanojia through Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) assistance of ₹37,000 per month along with 10% House Rent Allowance (HRA), with support commencing on 18 January 2024. 
 The financial assistance has helped him meet essential academic expenses, including tuition fees, study materials, accommodation and other educational requirements. It has eased the financial burden on his family and provided greater financial stability, enabling him to devote more attention to his studies and research. 
 Mr. Kanojia continues his academic pursuits with diligence, dedication and commitment. The fellowship has strengthened his confidence and aspiration to become self-reliant and fulfil his goals, while contributing meaningfully to his family, society and the nation. 
 The NFSC Scheme reflects the Government of India’s commitment to supporting eligible Scheduled Caste students in pursuing higher education and research. By extending financial assistance, the scheme helps students navigate economic barriers and work towards their academic and professional aspirations.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: From Informal Work To Dignified Employment
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 
 From Informal Work To Dignified Employment 
 NAMASTE Scheme Facilitates Formal Employment And Stability For A Sewer And Septic Tank Worker Raja of Manipur 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi 
 Mr Raja’s (name changed) journey highlights the importance of identifying and formally profiling sanitation workers and facilitating opportunities that promote dignified employment. 
 Through the NAMASTE Scheme, efforts are being made to move sanitation work towards mechanisation, safety, formalisation and improved livelihood opportunities for workers. 
 For many workers engaged in sewer and septic tank cleaning, informal employment arrangements often mean uncertain income, hazardous working conditions and limited access to occupational safety or formal recognition. 
 For Raja, a 27-year-old graduate from Manipur, securing dignified and stable employment marked an important step towards greater financial security and professional recognition. 
 Despite completing his graduation, Raja had been working in informal sewer and septic tank cleaning under contractor-based arrangements. His work was characterised by irregular earnings, limited occupational safety measures and the absence of formal employment benefits. With his household dependent on uncertain income, the lack of employment stability posed continuing challenges. 
 The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme seeks to formalise and improve the working conditions of Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) by facilitating their identification, profiling and access to support and opportunities. 
 Through formal profiling under the NAMASTE Scheme, Raja was recognised as a Sewer and Septic Tank Worker, helping facilitate an opportunity for institutional employment. 
 On October 15, 2025, Raja was engaged as a Skilled Daily Wage Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) Operator at the High Court of Manipur. The employment opportunity provided him with a more predictable source of income and improved recognition of his work and skills. 
 He now earns ₹480 per day, amounting to approximately ₹14,400 per month. The transition from irregular contractor-based work to a formal institutional engagement has brought greater income predictability and improved employment conditions, helping him work towards long-term financial stability. 
 His experience reflects how formal recognition and employment opportunities can help sanitation workers move beyond informal arrangements towards greater stability, dignity and professional security. 
 *****

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Data Security Council of India (DSCI) sign MoU to enable trusted data sharing for official statistics
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation 
 Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Data Security Council of India (DSCI) sign MoU to enable trusted data sharing for official statistics 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and the Data Security Council of India (DSCI), set up by Nasscom, a not-for-profit industry body and think tank on data protection and cyber security, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi today. Dr Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, Shri Vinayak Godse, Chief Executive Officer, DSCI, and senior officers of the Ministry were present on the occasion. The MoU forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen the National Statistical System through collaboration with public and private sector institutions. 
 Statistical agencies now-a-days use data from both traditional and alternative sources, some of which contain personal identifiers. With Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 scheduled to come into force in 2027, data producing agencies need to gear up themselves by reviewing how they handle such data while maintaining privacy and confidentiality. This partnership will help develop protocols for sharing data in trusted manner within and across agencies while maintaining data quality, protecting privacy and preserving statistical confidentiality. As a first step, MoSPI and DSCI will jointly prepare a policy paper on trusted data flows and data management, drawing on international good practices in data protection and cybersecurity. 
 The collaboration will also cover joint research on data governance and technical support for the adoption of privacy-enhancing technologies and the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). The MoU also provides facilitation for pilot projects with industry, academia, research institutions and international organisations and it will strengthen the national statistical ecosystem, by enabling responsible adoption of AI and emerging technologies.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation 
 Release of Report of the ‘Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts’ for the 2022-23 Series of National Accounts 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has undertaken the revision of the base year of National Accounts Statistics from 2011-12 to 2022-23. In this regard, the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS), under the chairmanship of Prof. B. N. Goldar, had decided FY 2022-23 as the new base year. Five Sub-Committees were constituted under ACNAS to deliberate on specific subject areas relating to the compilation and presentation of National Accounts Statistics. 
 i. Sub-Committee for Incorporation of New Data Sources, Rates and Ratios 
 ii. Sub-Committee for Methodological Improvements 
 iii. Sub-Committee for Constant Price Estimates 
 iv. Sub Committee on Regional Accounts 
 v. Sub-Committee for SNA 2025 Update 
 The Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts, was constituted to review the concepts, definitions, classifications, data sources and estimation methodologies for the compilation of State Domestic Product (SDP) and District Domestic Product (DDP). 
 The Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts, under the chairmanship of Prof. Ravindra H. Dholakia, Retired Professor, Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad , undertook a comprehensive review of the existing methodologies for the compilation of State and District Domestic Product estimates in the context of the revised base year 2022–23. The deliberations involved experts from academia, the Reserve Bank of India, Central Ministries and Departments, State and Union Territory Directorates of Economics and Statistics, NITI Aayog and officers of the National Statistics Office (NSO), MoSPI. 
 The Report of the Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts presents the deliberations and recommendations for improving the methodology for compilation of State Domestic Product estimates under all three approaches, namely, the Production Approach, Income Approach and Expenditure Approach , as well as the methodology for compilation of District Domestic Product (DDP) estimates. 
 Major Methodological Improvements includes: 
 Shift from allocation-based methods to direct estimation for some sectors or sub-sectors. 
 Reduction in reliance on fixed ratios and proxies. 
 Improved use of State-wise information of economic activity. 
 Greater methodological consistency across States. 
 The Uniform Guidelines for Compilation of Gross State Value Added (GSVA) under the Production Approach, as well as the Guidelines for Compilation of District Domestic Product (DDP), were uploaded on MoSPI’s website on 18.09.2026 and 03.06.2026, respectively, after incorporating suggestions received from stakeholders. 
 Further, the Draft Guidelines for Compilation of Gross State Value Added (GSVA) under the Expenditure Approach were uploaded on MoSPI’s website on 09.10.2026, inviting comments and suggestions from stakeholders by 28.10.2026. The final guidelines will be uploaded shortly after incorporating the suggestions received. 
 The Report is expected to serve as an important reference document for State and Union Territory Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DES) in strengthening their systems for compilation of State and District Domestic Product estimates under the revised base year series (2022–23). 
 The Report of the Sub-Committee on Regional Accounts is available on the official website of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation at https://mospi.gov.in/uploads/documents/ReportSubCommitteeOnRegionalAccounts.pdf . 
 ***** 
 Samrat
