Ministry of Women and Child Development 
 The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched #NumberSaveKiya? Campaign, released Advisory on 16 Days of activism against gender based violence & signed an inter-ministerial MoU for strengthening services for Women Safety at Nayi Chetna 5.0 
 Union Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi addressed the national campaign on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment on 25 November 2026 #NumberSaveKiya? campaign urged every woman to save Women Helpline 181 and Emergency 112 on her phone MoWCD, DoJ, NALSA and DoRD signed Joint MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:30PM by PIB Delhi 
 The Ministry of Women and Child Development joined the Ministry of Rural Development for the inauguration of Nayi Chetna 5.0 , the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment, on 25 November 2026 at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, PUSA, New Delhi. The event coincided with the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and the start of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. 
 The national event was graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister of Women and Child Development, along with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare, and Shri Kamlesh Paswan, Minister of State for Rural Development. 
 The Secretaries of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the Department of Rural Development also attended the event. 
 Key announcements 
 Advisory on the 16 Days campaign: The dignitaries released a Joint advisory issued by 10 Ministries and NALSA, guiding States and Union Territories to spread awareness, open access to support and legal aid, make women's safety everyone's responsibility, with the theme ‘From awareness to action & From access to agency’. 
 #NumberSaveKiya? Campaign: Built around one simple question, “Number save kiya?” (Have you saved the number?), the campaign video urged every woman, and those around her, to save the Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Support System 112 on their phones. Helpline 181 is a 24x7, toll-free service, linking women facing violence to police, One Stop Centres, medical care and legal aid. The campaign will be amplified through the Ministry’s digital platforms and its grassroots network of Anganwadi workers, One Stop Centres and Mission Shakti hubs. 
 Addressing the gathering, Smt. Annpurna Devi launched the #NumberSaveKiya? campaign and the Helpline Anthem, and urged everyone to save the Women Helpline 181, Emergency Helpline 112 and Child Helpline 1098 on their phones and to spread awareness among others. She said, “In this digital age, the mobile phone has become a great companion. In times of distress, a woman can get immediate help with just one call to a One Stop Centre, Gender Resource Centre or the Women Helpline near her. But sometimes, under extreme stress, she may not remember the number, and help may be delayed. Knowing the right information and the right contact number at the time of need can be the first step towards handling even the biggest difficulty. Our message through this campaign is: know the number, save the number and share it with others. I would like to ask each one of you, ‘Number save kiya?’” 
 Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages. He also encouraged everyone to save the Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Helpline 112 on their phones. 
 Inter-Ministerial MoU: An Inter-Ministerial MoU was signed by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Justice, NALSA and Department of Rural Development to launch the Violence-Free Village Initiative, bringing legal aid, women’s support services and community institutions together at the village level. 
 Convergence on the ground 
 The morning sessions featured two panel discussions: one on ministerial convergence through Gender Resource Centres, One Stop Centres, the Legal Services Authority and the health system, and another with women leaders from the field. New Gender Resource Centres were launched, and SHG leaders and One Stop Centre administrators shared their experiences. The event also saw the release of video resources and the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report, and the launch of the Nayi Chetna 5.0 Campaign. 
 As a part of Nayi Chetna 5.0, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, through its ‘Mission Shakti’, reaffirmed its commitment to the safety, security and empowerment of every woman. 
 **** 
 RC/SM

PIB Backgrounder 
 National Milk Day 
 “Celebrating India's Dairy Strength and Farmer Prosperity” 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 10:55AM by PIB Delhi 
 Milk at the Heart of India's Nutrition and Rural Economy 
 Milk occupies a vital place in India's nutritional landscape. It provides high-quality animal protein and essential nutrients, including calcium, magnesium and potassium, in easily absorbable forms. Often regarded as a near-complete food, milk supports growth, bone health and vitality across all age groups. 
 India has consistently remained the world's largest milk producer , contributing nearly one-fourth of global milk production . Between 2014-15 and 2024-25, production grew at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.41 percent , reaching 247.87 million tonnes . This growth also has a significant rural dimension. Dairying provides livelihoods to 8.5 crore rural households , with women playing a central role in milk production and collection. Nearly 70 percent of India’s dairy farming workforce comprises women , highlighting their contribution to the sector's growth and its role in promoting inclusive rural development. 
 Observed every year on 26 November , National Milk Day commemorates the birth anniversary of Dr. Verghese Kurien , the Father of India's White Revolution. The day recognises his transformative contribution to India's dairy cooperative movement. It honours the millions of dairy farmers whose efforts sustain the country's leadership in milk production. 
 India's Dairy Sector Records Strong Growth 
 India has maintained its position as the world's largest milk producer, supported by sustained growth in production and productivity. 
 Milk production increased by 69.41 percent, rising from 146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25 . 
 Leading milk-producing States were Uttar Pradesh ( 15.66 percent ), Rajasthan (14.82 percent), Madhya Pradesh (9.12 percent), Gujarat (7.78 percent), and Maharashtra (6.71 percent). These five States accounted for 54.09 percent of total Milk production in the country. 
 Per capita milk availability rose by 52.03 percent , from 319 grams per person per day in 2014-15 to 485 grams in 2024-25 . 
 Average bovine milk productivity increased from 1,640 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15 to 2,800 kg per animal per year in 2024-25 , registering growth of 69 percent. 
 The Cooperative Strength Behind India's Milk Economy 
 India's dairy cooperative movement provides an organised platform for milk producers. It connects village-level societies with district milk unions and State federations. These institutions support milk procurement, processing, marketing, and access to dairy services. 
 To explore the historical journey of India's dairy sector: Click Here 
 The country's dairy cooperative network comprises: 
 22 milk federations. 
 241 district cooperative milk unions. 
 28 marketing dairies. 
 25 Milk Producer Organisations. 
 Coverage of approximately 2.45 lakh villages and 1.65 crore dairy farmers as members. 
 The network provides an institutional link between rural milk producers and organised dairy markets. It also supports collective marketing and access to better organised milk procurement systems. 
 NDDB Dairy Services 
 The National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) has played an important role in developing farmer-owned dairy institutions in India. Its wholly owned, not-for-profit subsidiary, NDDB Dairy Services (NDDB-DS) , facilitates the incorporation and operationalisation of Milk Producer Organisations (MPOs). 
 MPOs are farmer-owned Producer Companies that organise milk producers into professionally managed institutions. They facilitate collective milk procurement, strengthen market linkages, and provide farmers access to transparent pricing and direct bank payments. 
 As of 31 October 2026, 
 NDDB-DS has successfully established 25 MPOs . 
 18 of these 25 MPOs have all-women membership, with women serving as all the producer directors on their respective boards. 
 These organisations cover more than 13 lakh milk producers across 175 districts in 12 States . 
 Women constitute around 78 percent of the producers in these organisations. 
 The MPOs procure around 70 lakh litres of milk per day . 
 Milk Procurement and Sales by Dairy Cooperatives 
 Dairy cooperatives provide an organised market for farmers and help ensure regular procurement of milk. Procurement prices are decided by the cooperatives and other dairies, based on production costs and market conditions. Many dairy cooperatives use automated milk collection and payment systems. Payments are credited directly to farmers' bank accounts. 
 As on 31 October 2026 , dairy cooperatives recorded: 
 690.90 lakh kg per day of milk procurement. 
 462.95 lakh litres per day of liquid milk sales. 
 A New Momentum for Dairy Cooperatives 
 White Revolution 2.0, a cooperative-led initiative formally launched on 25 December 2024 (SOP launched on 19 September 2024) aims to expand dairy cooperative coverage in uncovered villages and Panchayats. It seeks to increase milk procurement by dairy cooperatives by 50 percent over the next five years. The initiative focuses on strengthening the cooperative network, improving market access, generating employment, and promoting women's empowerment. The activities envisaged under White Revolution 2.0 are funded under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD). 
 By 2028-29, the initiative aims to establish 75,000 new Dairy Cooperative Societies in uncovered villages and Panchayats and strengthen 46,422 existing Dairy Cooperative Societies .

 24,097 new Dairy Cooperative Societies formed. 
 31,394 existing Dairy Cooperative Societies strengthened.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
PIB Backgrounder 
 Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 
 Thirukkural Payilvom: Taking the Thirukkural to Campuses Across India 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 9:41AM by PIB Delhi 
 Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the longstanding cultural, linguistic and civilisational ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi (Varanasi), reflecting the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat. The fifth edition, scheduled from 28 November to 12 December 2026, will focus on the theme “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen” , promoting the timeless teachings of the Thirukkural among young learners. Around 1,400 delegates from Tamil Nadu will visit Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya. A nationwide Students’ Engagement Programme will involve 1,000 Higher Education Institutions, while teachers from Tamil Nadu will introduce the Thirukkural in schools and colleges in Uttar Pradesh. Through academic exchanges, cultural programmes and multilingual outreach, the initiative seeks to deepen mutual understanding, strengthen people-to-people connections and promote India’s shared heritage. 
 About Kashi Tamil Sangamam 
 Kashi Tamil Sangamam celebrates the age-old civilisational bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, the two ancient seats of learning. Many people from the two states have visited Kashi and Rameswaram as part of their religious traditions, reflecting the cultural bonds between the northern and southern parts of India. 
 Many people from Tamil Nadu have lived around Hanuman Ghat and Kedar Ghat for generations. Swami Kumaragurupara of Dharmapuram Adheenam came to Kashi from Tamil Nadu and built the Kedareshwar Temple at Kedar Ghat. The 200-year-old Kumaraswamy Mutt and Markandeya Ashram are situated at the same ghat. Tenkasi in Tamil Nadu is called the Kashi of the South. Banaras Hindu University has a chair dedicated to Mahakavi Subramania Bharati. 
 The broader objective of the Sangamam, set out when it was announced in 2022, is to bring the two knowledge and cultural traditions closer, create an understanding of shared heritage and deepen the people-to-people bond between the regions. 
 The first Kashi Tamil Sangamam was held in 2022, during Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav. Over its four editions, it has facilitated exchanges of knowledge, language, traditions and lived experiences between the two regions. The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has called it a "vibrant programme which deepens the spirit of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat'". 
 In each edition, students, teachers, artisans, scholars, spiritual leaders and cultural practitioners from Tamil Nadu have spent a week to ten days in Kashi. They have visited the temples of Kashi, places with Tamil links and the nearby cities of Ayodhya and Prayagraj. The participants also met their Kashi counterparts at seminars, talks, cultural programmes, sporting events and exhibitions. 
 The Sangamam is organised by the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras, Banaras Hindu University, the Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Chennai, and the Government of Uttar Pradesh. Several Central Ministries and Departments are also partners, among them Culture, Railways, Tourism and Textiles. 
 Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0: Thirukkural Payilvom 
 The fifth edition of the Sangamam will be held from 28 November to 12 December 2026 on the theme "Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen" (Let's Learn Thirukkural). 
 The Thirukkural is the classical Tamil text of ethics and conduct. Its author, Thiruvalluvar, set it in three parts: Aram (virtue) , Porul (wealth) , and Inbam (love) . The text has 1,330 couplets , and CICT has translated it into 25 Indian languages including all 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution, in addition to several foreign languages and braille. 
 The aims of the fifth edition are: 
 • To bring the ethical and moral wisdom of the Thirukkural closer to the youth and to learners across the country. 
 • To encourage the reading, understanding and application of the values of the text in everyday life, through educational engagement, multilingual resources and wider public outreach. 
 • To promote wider understanding of the Thirukkural among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. 
 Key Initiatives of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 
 Students' Engagement Programme 
 A nationwide Students' Engagement Programme will be undertaken through 1,000 Higher Education Institutions to promote wider understanding of the Thirukkural among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. It will include structured study, research and campus-based activities. 
 •Each participating institution will assess its interested students on the Thirukkural and nominate one student on merit. 
 •The selected students will attend an online academic orientation, offered in the 22 scheduled languages and in English. 
 •A one-month research and academic engagement will follow, with multilingual study material from CICT. Each eligible selected student will be entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and completion of the prescribed requirements. 
 •Each student will write an article or research note of 4 to 10 pages under a faculty guide, and give a one-hour presentation on the Thirukkural at the institution. 
 Thirukkural Teaching in Schools and Colleges of Uttar Pradesh 
 During the Sangamam, 50 teachers from Tamil Nadu will visit Uttar Pradesh and teach the Thirukkural in schools and colleges. Thirukkural experts from Tamil Nadu will also visit schools and colleges in Varanasi. They will introduce students to the core values of the text through orientation modules, interactive sessions and quizzes. 
 Reading Sessions in Schools 
 The National Book Trust, in association with the Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya, will conduct interactive sessions in schools in Varanasi on reading habits, storytelling and creative activities. 
 Inauguration, Conference and Cultural Programme

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Major Step by India Towards Self-Reliance in Urea Production; 6 New Plants Approved
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : 
Department of Fertilizers 
 Major Step by India Towards Self-Reliance in Urea Production; 6 New Plants Approved 
 6 New Urea Plants to be Set Up in the Country under the National Investment policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026; The Goal Is Self-Reliance in Urea Production An Investment of ₹54,000 Crore, Domestic Urea Expansion Targets Self-Reliance 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi 
 Aligned with the Vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat of Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri. Narendra Modi, the Government of India has taken a decisive step toward strengthening agricultural resilience, ensuring fertilizer security, and achieving self-reliance ( Atmanirbharta ) in urea production. Approving 6 new urea plants in brownfield category under the national investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026—with more projects to follow—the initiative focuses on self-reliance in urea manufacturing with an investment of approximately ₹54,000 crore. 
 Focus on 6 New brownfield Plants, Investment, and Self-Reliance: 
 Under the National investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026, 6 key brownfield urea projects have been taken forward across public sector, private sector, and cooperative enterprises: 
 MFL-Madras (Chennai, Tamil Nadu): A PSU brownfield project with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT to replace the existing unit, which is over 60 years old that incurs higher production costs, high energy consumption, and safety hazards. Old plant being non-efficient needs to be replaced. 
 NFL Nangal (Nangal, Punjab): A PSU brownfield replacement of a legacy PSU plant, around 50-55 years old, with present production capacity of 4.73 LMT/annum by a modern unit with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT. 
 KFL-Shahjahanpur (Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh): A cooperative brownfield project (KRIBHCO) expanding the unit commissioned in 1995, with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT. 
 Matix-Panagarh (Panagarh, West Bengal): A private brownfield project building with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT on an existing modern plant commissioned in 2017. So far, West Bengal has only one urea plant. New plant will support the requirement of the State. 
 CFCL Gadepan (Gadepan, Kota, Rajasthan): A private brownfield project expanding at the complex operational since 1994, with an annual installed production capacity of 12.7 LMT. 
 IIPL-Jagdishpur (Jagdishpur, Uttar Pradesh): A private brownfield project proposing a 12.7 LMT/annum capacity addition at the plant established in 1988. 
 Capitalizing on brownfield advantages—such as existing land, utilities, infrastructure, logistics, and technical manpower—will enable faster execution and cost efficiency, while additional projects in the pipeline will further advance self-reliance. 
 Connection to Aging Plants and Replacement: 
 Legacy urea units—such as MFL-Madras (over 60 years old) and NFL Nangal (around 50–55 years old)—face higher production costs, elevated energy consumption, and process-safety risks. For instance, Nangal operates at 6.498 Gcal/MT compared to the weighted industry average of 5.95 Gcal/MT and the New Energy Norm of 5 Gcal/MT. Replacing and modernizing aging, energy-intensive units through brownfield expansion addresses safety and efficiency challenges while sustaining domestic urea supply. 
 Impact Against Consumption and Import Reduction: 
 India's annual urea demand/consumption stands at around 400 LMT (Lakh Metric Tonnes). Domestic urea production increased from 225 LMT per annum in 2014–15 to a record 314.07 LMT in 2023–24 and stood at 293.30 LMT during 2025–26, while total indigenous Reassessed Capacity (RAC) rose from 207.54 LMTPA in 2014–15 to 269.42 LMTPA during 2026–27. With fresh capacity additions and expansion plans measured against an annual consumption of around 400 LMT, reliance on imported urea is set to decrease substantially, saving foreign exchange and strengthening domestic availability. 
 Poised to Unlock ₹54,000 Crore Investment 
 With each brownfield project estimated at a capital cost norm of around ₹9,000 crore, the 6 urea plants are poised to attract nearly ₹54,000 crore in fresh investment, advancing India toward self-reliance ( Atmanirbharta ) in urea production while generating employment. To strengthen investor confidence and project bankability, the framework pairs a balanced 12–16% Return on Equity (RoE) band—anchored by a 12% floor and a 16% ceiling—with a foreign exchange rate mitigation mechanism that normalizes exchange rates and converts into INR after four years based on prevailing rates. Coupled with brownfield advantages that deliver an estimated ₹225 crore in annual savings—or roughly ₹1,800 crore over eight years—these provisions enhance financial viability and drive sustained capital inflows into domestic fertilizer manufacturing. 
 Success of New Investment Policy (NIP)-2012 and Detailed Outlook of India's Urea Policies: 
 Announced on 2 nd January 2013 and amended on 7 th October 2014, New Investment Policy-2012 led to the setting up of 6 new urea manufacturing units—4 through Joint Venture Companies (JVC) of nominated PSUs (Ramagundam unit of RFCL in Telangana; and Gorakhpur, Sindri, and Barauni units of HURL in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar, respectively) and 2 by private companies (Panagarh unit of Matix Fertilizers in West Bengal and Gadepan-III unit of Chambal Fertilizers in Rajasthan). Each unit has a 12.7 LMTPA production capacity, together adding 76.2 LMTPA and raising total indigenous RAC from 207.54 LMTPA in 2014–15 to 269.42 LMTPA in 2026–27. In addition, two 12.7 LMTPA projects are under execution: Talcher Fertilizer Project (TFL) in Odisha via coal-gasification route (expected to complete by December 2027) and Assam Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Company Limited (AVFCCL) at Namrup, Assam (announced on 19th March 2025). 
 *** 
 Neeraj Kumar Bhatt 
 cmc.fertilizers[at]gmail[dot]com

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Culture 
 Nehru Science Centre, Mumbai, to Host Western Zonal National Science Drama Competition 2026–27 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Mumbai : 25 November 2026 
 Nehru Science Centre, Mumbai, a constituent unit of the National Council of Science Museums (NCSM), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, is set to host the Western Zonal National Science Drama Competition 2026–27 on 27 November 2026. The competition will bring together talented student teams from six states and one Union Territory, using theatre as a creative medium to explore scientific ideas and their relevance to society. 
 Organised under the theme “Science & Society,” the competition aims to make science engaging, relatable and thought-provoking through dramatic performances. The participating teams, selected through state-level competitions, will represent Chhattisgarh, Goa, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. 
 The National Science Drama Festival is one of NCSM's flagship educational initiatives, encouraging students to explore science beyond textbooks through acting, storytelling, creativity and teamwork. The competition progresses through Taluka, District and State levels, culminating in zonal competitions across the country, with selected teams advancing to the national level. 
 The student teams will present science-based plays in Hindi on contemporary subjects including AI: Friend, Tool or Threat? EV – The Way Forward; Interstellar Habitats; and Restoring Oceans – Preserving Generations. Through these performances, students will examine scientific advancements, environmental concerns, technological possibilities and their impact on human life and the future of society. 
 The competition is organised in collaboration with the State Council of Educational Research & Training (SCERT), Chhattisgarh; SCERT, Goa; Rajya Shiksha Kendra, Madhya Pradesh; Regional Academic Authority, SISE, Maharashtra; Department of Science & Technology, Rajasthan; and the Department of Science & Technology, Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. 
 The inaugural ceremony will be held at 9:30 AM, with Shri Rajendra Butala, renowned theatre personality, actor, producer, director and mimicry artist from Mumbai, as the Chief Guest. The event will culminate in a valedictory ceremony and prize distribution at 6:30 PM, graced by Ms. Aruna Raje Patil, renowned Indian film director and editor, Mumbai. 
 An eminent jury comprising Ms. Aparna Dharmadhikari, Mr. Nilay Vaidya and Mr. Satpute will adjudicate the performances based on scientific content, script, creativity, acting, presentation and overall impact. 
 Nehru Science Centre, Mumbai, through this festival, seeks to foster scientific temper, encourage creative expression and provide a vibrant platform for students from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds to interact, collaborate and share ideas. By blending science with performing arts, the initiative makes scientific learning more experiential, enjoyable and meaningful. The festival underscores the message that science and art are integral part of everyday life and a vital force in shaping an informed, progressive and sustainable society.

Ministry of Defence 
 National Academy of Defence Production (NADP), Nagpur Celebrates its Historic Second PGDM Convocation 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:01PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Nagpur : 25 November 2026 
 The National Academy of Defence Production (NADP), Nagpur, celebrated the Second Convocation Ceremony of its PGDM (Business Management) Programme 2024-26 Batch , at Utsav Hall, marking another significant milestone in its mission of developing future-ready leaders for India's defence and manufacturing sectors. 
 The ceremony was graced by Shri Sanjay Hazari, Chairman & Managing Director, Munitions India Limited (MIL) , as the Chief Guest. In his inspiring Convocation Address, Shri Hazari described the graduating students as torchbearers of India's strategic future and called upon them to contribute meaningfully towards the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat through innovation, integrity, and professional excellence. 
 Highlighting the unique strengths of the programme, Shri Hazari commended NADP's PGDM (BM) curriculum, mentored by IIM Indore and enriched with learning resources from Harvard Business Publishing . He appreciated the Academy's emphasis on leadership development, emotional intelligence, sustainability, and industry-oriented learning, describing it as a model for future-ready management education in the defence sector. 
 With a total batch size of 27 students, the convocation honored the graduating students who successfully completed the AICTE-approved, two-year residential PGDM (BM) program with a focus on defence and business management. Shri Bhuvnesh Verma, Additional General Manager, Ordnance Factory Varangaon , a sponsored candidate of MIL, was awarded the Gold Medal as the First Topper, while Shri Hrushikesh S. Payghan secured the Silver Medal as the Second Topper in recognition of their outstanding academic performance and leadership qualities. 
 The programme has delivered impressive outcomes, achieving 100% internship opportunities and 76% placement success . Graduates have secured positions in reputed organizations including NKRF, Aiila Innovation, ideaForge, Dhruva Aerospace, Siddhi Engineers, Jane's Defence India LLP, Gairesh Logistics, Tetrahedron, Piersight, and Divyanshi Aviation. The students also underwent internships with leading organizations such as ITC, Larsen & Toubro (L&T), Indorama Synthetics Pvt. Ltd., KPMG, Indian Bank, L&T Energy Hydrocarbon, Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL), DelaPlex Ltd., Bharat Forge Ltd., Jindal Defence Systems Pvt. Ltd., Jayaswal Neco Industries Ltd., TIOT Systems Pvt. Ltd., Quincare Pharmaceuticals Pvt. Ltd., Boltcargo India Pvt. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: FSSAI West Region Organised Mega Street Food Vendors Training and Awareness Programme under Seva Saptah 2026 at Shegaon
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 FSSAI West Region Organised Mega Street Food Vendors Training and Awareness Programme under Seva Saptah 2026 at Shegaon 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:26PM by PIB Mumbai 
 PIB Mumbai | 24 November 2026 
 The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), West Region, organised a Street Food Vendors Training and Awareness Programme under Seva Saptah 2026 on 24 November 2026 at Shri Sant Gajanan Maharaj College of Engineering (SSGMCE), Shegaon, District Buldhana, Maharashtra. The programme witnessed an overwhelming response, with more than 1,500 participants comprising street food vendors, women entrepreneurs, local citizens and other stakeholders attending the event. 
 The programme was graced by the presence of the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, as the Chief Guest. The Regional Director, FSSAI, West Region, Pritee Chaudhary, the Principal of SSGMCE, Dr. S.B. Soami; along with other senior district officials and dignitaries, were also present. 
 Addressing the gathering, Hon’ble Minister of State Shri Prataprao Jadhav emphasised that food safety is a shared responsibility and highlighted the importance of maintaining cleanliness, hygiene and quality in food preparation. He encouraged street food vendors to adopt safe food handling practices and contribute towards the vision of a healthier India. 
 The Regional Director, FSSAI, West Region, Pritee Chaudhary, highlighted FSSAI's initiatives to strengthen food safety at the grassroots level. She encouraged street food vendors to adopt hygienic practices, obtain the requisite FSSAI registration and make food safety an integral part of their daily business operations. 
 The Principal of SSGMCE, in his address, appreciated FSSAI's initiative to organise the programme at Shegaon and emphasised the role of educational institutions in creating awareness about public health, food safety and community welfare. He welcomed the dignitaries and participants and expressed his institution's support for such meaningful initiatives. 
 The programme focused on essential aspects of food safety, including personal hygiene, sanitation, safe food preparation and storage, prevention of food contamination, cleanliness at food vending premises and compliance with the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Participants were also sensitised about FSSAI registration and licensing requirements and various initiatives undertaken by the Authority along with the knowledge of financial literacy. 
 The large-scale participation of more than 1,500 people reflected the strong community response towards food safety awareness and capacity-building initiatives. The programme aimed to empower street food vendors and women entrepreneurs with practical knowledge and skills to ensure safe and hygienic food for consumers.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 AIIMS Nagpur Organises PAN-CME 2026 on Pancreatic Cancer, Bringing Together 150+ Medical Professionals 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:35PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Nagpur : 25 November 2026 
 The Department of Surgical Gastroenterology, All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Nagpur, in association with the Gastrointestinal Surgeons Forum, Nagpur (GIS Forum) and the Association of Surgeons Nagpur (ASN), organised PAN-CME 2026 – Practical Approach to Neoplasms of the Pancreas – on 14 November 2026 at AIIMS Nagpur, to mark Pancreatic Cancer Awareness Month. 
 More than 150 delegates participated in the CME. Eminent faculty from PGIMER Chandigarh, Tata Memorial Hospital Mumbai, AIIMS New Delhi, AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Rishikesh, Nizam's Institute Hyderabad and other leading institutions attended the programme. Senior surgeons, surgical oncologists, gastroenterologists, radiologists and trainees from Nagpur and nearby regions also participated. 
 The CME was inaugurated by Prof. Prashant P. Joshi, Executive Director, AIIMS Nagpur. In his address, Prof. Joshi highlighted pancreatic cancer as an important and challenging abdominal malignancy. He emphasised early diagnosis, timely surgery and the appropriate use of neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy. He also spoke about government initiatives to make cancer treatment more affordable, including recent measures to reduce the prices of anticancer medicines. 
 During the inaugural ceremony, Dr Sudhir Madhukar Tomey and Dr Shrikant Mukewar were felicitated by the Executive Director for their pioneering and exemplary contributions to Surgical Gastroenterology and Medical Gastroenterology, respectively, in Central India. 
 The scientific sessions covered the evaluation of pancreatic tumours, multidisciplinary treatment planning, surgical advances, perioperative care, management of postoperative complications and newer oncological therapies. Expert lectures, operative videos and case-based panel discussions focused on practical decision-making and improving patient outcomes. 
 The speakers included Dr Puneet Dhar, Dr Udit Chauhan, Dr Rajesh Gupta, Dr Chetan Kantharia, Dr Manoj Vyawahare, Dr Rajesh Panwar, Dr Kalayarasan Raja, Dr Vikram A. Chaudhari, Dr Vaibhav Varshney and Dr Kamal Bandhate. 
 Dr Nirjhar Raj Rakesh, Organising Chairperson and In-Charge, Department of Surgical Gastroenterology, AIIMS Nagpur, presented the journey of the department. He shared that the department was established in 2022 and has developed into a specialised unit performing major abdominal cancer surgeries, with a particular focus on complex pancreatic surgery. 
 The core organising committee included Dr Nirjhar Raj Rakesh, Dr Mohanasundaram A., Dr Manpreet Uppal, Dr Prachiti Gokhe, Dr Makrand, Mr Vishal Chhatrashal and Mr Ashwin Bhaisare. The programme received guidance and support from Dr Sudhir Madhukar Tomey, Dr Yogesh Bang, Dr Ayush and Dr Rajvilas of the GIS Forum, and Dr Praveen Vairagade of the Association of Surgeons Nagpur.The organisers thanked the national faculty, senior clinicians, chairpersons, panellists, delegates, residents and supporting staff for making PAN-CME 2026 successful.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Krishnavataram brings Lord Krishna’s life to the screen through Satyabhama’s eyes 
 First part of a three-film series explores love, devotion, and lesser-known chapters of Krishna’s life 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 8:00PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 Makers of the Hindi feature film Krishnavataram (Krishnavataram Part 1: The Heart), screened under the Indian Panorama Feature Films section at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, addressed a press conference organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) today. Director Hardik Gajjar and producer Sajan Raj Kurup shared insights on bringing a visually enriched, contemporary cinematic interpretation of Lord Krishna’s life to global audiences. 
 Speaking on the core idea behind the film, producer Sajan Raj Kurup said that in India, Lord Krishna cannot be boxed into the category of mythology. “Krishna in India is beyond mythology. This is faith, an emotion, and a living part of our history,” he remarked. Raised in a cultural tradition centred around Adikeshava, he recalled the belief that “everything comes from Krishna,” adding that the team worked deliberately to portray his life with sincerity and deep respect. 
 The filmmakers also shared that Krishnavataram is the first chapter of a three-part trilogy built around Heart, Mind, and Soul. Adapted from Raam Mori’s novel Satyabhama , with a screenplay by Prakash Kapadia, Raam Mori, and Hardik Gajjar and drawing on the Srimad Bhagavatam and Harivamsa , the opening part follows Krishna’s journey from Vrindavan and Mathura to his rule in Dwarka through Satyabhama’s eyes. While Part 1 centres on love, sacrifice, separation, and devotion, the next two parts will examine his statecraft and strategy (The Mind) and the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita (The Soul ). Featuring lesser-known episodes from Krishna’s life, the film stars Siddharth Gupta, Sanskruti Jayana, Sushmitha Bhat, and Nivaashiyni Krishnan play key roles. 
 Addressing the need to connect traditional narratives with modern viewers, director Hardik Gajjar explained that the movie is specially built for the younger generation so they can discover and relate to their history in an engaging cinematic language. “Storytelling can keep on changing, and we are fortunate to live in a time where we can create visually enriched experiences,” the makers shared. Drawing on Gajjar’s visual effects background and built on a massive 7.5 acre set with some of the best talent working on VFX, the film has been made in multiple languages, including English, specifically to resonate with young people worldwide. 
 Highlighting the pivotal role of the soundtrack in driving emotional connection, Gajjar spoke about collaborating with music director Prasad S. Under the guidance of renowned maestro Dr. Bharat Balvalli, the team included as much classical music as they could, seamlessly blending traditional purity with a contemporary touch to connect with today’s audience. 
 The session was moderated by Shri. Sandeep Prasad.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Tago Explores the Search for Home, Human Fragility and the Consequences of Force; Makes World Premiere at 57th IFFI
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 
 Tago Explores the Search for Home, Human Fragility and the Consequences of Force; Makes World Premiere at 57th IFFI 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Mumbai 
 Goa, 25 November 2026 
 Addressing a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, director Aleksandr Anisimov and co-screenplay writer Veronika Oznobishina spoke about Tago , which had its World Premiere at the festival in the Cinema of the World section. Made with non-professional actors drawn from local communities and set against Georgia's natural landscapes, the film explores the search for home and belonging, human fragility, gender dynamics and the consequences of responding to conflict through force. 
 Set in a remote Georgian village surrounded by mist-covered mountains, the story begins when a local man discovers the body of a young stranger on a riverbank and brings him home to his wife and young son. The unexpected arrival disrupts the family's already fragile existence, setting off a chain of events that compels its members to make difficult and extreme choices. 
 Speaking about the film's portrayal of gender dynamics and the emotional confinement experienced by its female protagonist, Oznobishina said, "The very first thing we wanted to show was that the woman lives in a cage within her own house, while the man fails to understand the predicament she faces in her everyday life." 
 She explained that the film also follows the upheavals confronting the male protagonist, whose response is driven by an overwhelming surge of energy that prevents him from making the right choices. She emphasised the importance of inner resilience and the strength required to confront unfavourable circumstances. 
 Anisimov spoke about the protagonist's approach to conflict, observing that he chooses to resolve his problems in the old-fashioned way, through force. Drawing parallels with human behaviour across societies, he noted that people often resort to force when faced with difficult situations. The film examines the consequences of such choices and questions whether force can resolve life's complex problems. 
 The film took shape during Anisimov's travels across Georgia, where he observed the lives of ordinary people, their motivations and the circumstances shaping their experiences. During one such journey, he encountered a Georgian theatre actor, and the two joined hands to bring the story to the screen. They decided to cast non-professional actors from local communities, making the participation of local residents central to the project. 
 Anisimov discovered the film's female lead, Magdalena Bolqvadze, at a bus stop. Something in her persona suggested a tragic story to him, prompting him to envision how the camera could capture that emotion without filters. This chance encounter eventually led to her casting in the film. 
 The team also recorded hundreds of videos of local residents before finalising the cast. Working with a modest budget, the filmmakers gradually involved more people from the surrounding communities. Anisimov expressed particular gratitude to the people of Georgia, whose generosity and support included providing costumes and helping the crew with logistical arrangements. 
 Actor Egor Skorokhodov, who also comes from a non-professional acting background, shared that he connected with the director by chance and subsequently became part of the filmmaking journey. 
 The team expressed happiness at presenting the film at IFFI, appreciating the opportunity to watch films from across the world and engage with diverse cinematic voices. 
 The press conference was moderated by Sandeep Sunil.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Manager Marketing, Telangana State Shri S. KARUPPAIAH organized PM-PRANAM - Kissan Sangosthi at Telangana State
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers 
 Manager Marketing, Telangana State Shri S. KARUPPAIAH organized PM-PRANAM - Kissan Sangosthi at Telangana State 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 4:50PM by PIB Hyderabad 
 Madras Fertilizers Limited, Hyderabad organized PM-PRANAM - Kissan Sangosthi for Paddy farmers at Rythumithra Seeds, Village Damaracherla, Mandal Damaracherla, District Nalgonda, Telangana State on 25-11-2026 from 11.00 AM to 4.00 PM. 
 The programme was organized by Manager Marketing, Telangana State Shri S. KARUPPAIAH. 
 23 Paddy farmers participated in the programme and were benefited. 
 The main objective of the programme was to create awareness among Paddy farmers on PM PRANAM Scheme of Government of India, Balanced Fertilizer Usage in Paddy, Use of Organic Manure in Paddy, Soil Health Management for Paddy and Role of PMKSK Centres. 
 Importance of Kisan Sangoshthi: 
 Kisan Sangoshthi is an important platform for direct interaction between Company, Agriculture Department and Paddy Farmers. In this programme, Paddy farmers were explained about modern cultivation practices, correct dose of fertilizers, and Government schemes in simple language. 
 The programme helped Paddy farmers to understand the importance of Soil Health Card and soil testing before fertilizer application in Paddy, know the correct time and method of fertilizer application in Paddy - Basal, Tillering and Panicle Initiation stages, reduce unnecessary expenditure on chemical fertilizers, and increase Paddy yield and income through balanced nutrition. 
 Importance of PM PRANAM Scheme: 
 PM PRANAM (PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth) scheme was explained in detail to Paddy farmers. 
 Key points explained:
- To reduce the use of chemical fertilizers and promote use of organic / bio fertilizers and organic manure in Paddy.
- To promote sustainable agriculture and protect soil health.
- To reduce subsidy burden and protect Mother Earth.
- To encourage use of Nano Urea, Nano DAP, Bio-fertilizers, City Compost and Vermicompost in Paddy.
- States / Districts reducing chemical fertilizer consumption will be incentivized by Government of India. 
 Paddy farmers were advised to adopt Integrated Nutrient Management - combination of chemical fertilizers, organic manure and bio-fertilizers for better soil health and higher Paddy yield. 
 PMKSK Centre - Importance: 
 PMKSK (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendra) Centres were explained as One Stop Solution for Paddy farmers. 
 Services available at PMKSK Centre:
- Availability of all fertilizers - Urea, DAP, MOP, NPK, SSP etc. at Government fixed price for Paddy.
- Availability of Paddy Seeds, Pesticides and Agri Inputs.
- Soil Testing facility and Soil Health Card.
- Advisory on Paddy crop, fertilizer and pest management.
- Display of Information on Government Schemes.
- Availability of MFL Vijay Products - Vijay Urea, Vijay DAP, Vijay NPK, Vijay MOP, Vijay City Compost etc. for Paddy. 
 Farmers were requested to purchase fertilizers only from PMKSK Centres / Authorized Dealers and to take proper bill. 
 Soil Health - Importance for Paddy: 
 Soil Health was the main topic of discussion for Paddy crop. 
 Farmers were explained that soil is the foundation of Paddy cultivation. If soil health is lost, Paddy yield will come down. Continuous use of only Urea / DAP without organic manure damages soil structure. Soil testing should be done once in 2 years and fertilizers should be applied as per Soil Health Card recommendations for Paddy. 
 Use of Organic Manure, Green Manure, Vermicompost and Bio-fertilizers improves soil organic carbon, water holding capacity and micro-organisms in Paddy fields. Balanced use of NPK + Secondary and Micronutrients like Zinc, Boron, Sulphur is essential for good Paddy yield. Zinc deficiency is common in Paddy fields of Nalgonda area. 
 Farmers were advised to avoid burning of Paddy straw, use it as compost to improve soil health, and to do Green Manuring with Dhaincha / Sunhemp before Paddy transplanting to improve soil fertility. 
 Recommended Fertilizer Schedule for Paddy - Explained:
Stage Fertilizer
Basal / Transplanting DAP / NPK + Zinc Sulphate + Organic Manure
Tillering Stage (20-25 DAT) Urea + MOP
Panicle Initiation Stage (45-50 DAT) Urea + MOP
Grain Filling Stage Nano Urea Spray if required
Farmers were advised not to apply excess Urea in one dose. Split application gives better result. 
 Arrangements Made: 
 - Banner of Kisan Sangoshthi : PM PRANAM was displayed prominently at the venue.
- MFL Standee was displayed at the venue for visibility and awareness on MFL Vijay Products, PM PRANAM and Soil Health.
- Sweets were distributed to all participating farmers.
- Drinking Water was arranged for all farmers and officials.
- Cool Drinks were arranged and served to all participants. 
 Paddy farmers actively participated and raised queries on availability of fertilizers in Rabi Paddy season, price of fertilizers, use of Nano Urea in Paddy, soil testing procedure, Zinc deficiency in Paddy and MFL products availability at PMKSK Centre. All queries were answered by MFL Officers and Agriculture Department Officials. 
 The programme concluded successfully. Farmers understood the importance of PM PRANAM, Balanced Fertilization and Soil Health for Paddy. Farmers assured to use Organic Manure along with chemical fertilizers in Paddy and to purchase fertilizers from PMKSK Centre. Good rapport developed between MFL, Dealer and Paddy Farmers of Damaracherla area. 
 Issued By: 
 (S. KARUPPAIAH)
Manager Marketing, Telangana State
Madras Fertilizers Limited, 
 ***

Special Service and Features 
 CCRS to Organize National Conference on Siddha for Global Health in Chennai 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 7:38PM by PIB Chennai 
 The Central Council for Research in Siddha (CCRS), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, is organizing a two-day National Conference on Siddha for Global Health (NCSGH) on November 26 and 27, 2026, bringing together approximately 1,000 delegates, including researchers, academicians, Siddha practitioners and students, to deliberate on scientific advancements, clinical applications and the global relevance of the Siddha system of medicine. 
 The conference will be held at the Central Auditorium, Institute of Asian Studies, Sholinganallur, Chennai. It aims to provide a national platform for scientific discussions, exchange of research findings and exploration of Siddha medicine’s contributions to contemporary healthcare. 
 The scientific programme will feature expert presentations on the integration of Siddha with modern healthcare, clinical applications, toxicogenomics, reproductive health and the global positioning of Siddha medicine. The sessions are expected to encourage interdisciplinary dialogue and highlight the potential of Siddha research in addressing contemporary healthcare challenges. 
 Among the key scientific presentations, Dr. Kapil S. Sarde, Expert in Modern Medicine and Non-Official Member of the General Body, CCRS, will speak on “Clinical Application of Integrated Medicine in the Current Healthcare Scenario, with Special Emphasis on the Siddha System of Medicine.” 
 Dr. V. Balamurugan, Siddha Physician, Amrutha Centre for Siddha Medicine, will present “Clinical Gunapadam from a Toxicogenomics Standpoint.” Dr. G. Shankar, Siddha Physician and Fertility Consultant, Ezhil Siddha Hospital, will address “In Between Pink Lines: The Disease, the Burden, the Pride and the Stigma.” Dr. S. Natarajan, Research Officer, CCRS, will speak on “Positioning Siddha in Global Health: Terminologies, Classifications and Interoperability.” 
 The inaugural programme will commence with a welcome address by Dr. S. Selvarajan, Research Officer (Siddha)/Scientist-IV, CCRS. The keynote address will be delivered by Prof. Dr. N. J. Muthukumar, Director General, CCRS, followed by felicitation by Dr. A. Rajendra Kumar, Research Officer (Siddha)/Scientist-III. 
 Dr. Kapil S. Sarde will attend as the Guest of Honor. Special addresses will be delivered by Dr. John Samuel, Founder, Institute of Asian Studies, and Dr H.Mubarak, Assistant Adviser (Siddha), 
 Ministry of Ayush, Dr. A. Kanagarajan, Research Officer (Siddha)/Scientist-IV, CCRS, will deliver the vote of thanks.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: IIT Madras to Host National ‘eCV Dialogue’ to Accelerate Commercial Vehicle Electrification
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Special Service and Features 
 IIT Madras to Host National ‘eCV Dialogue’ to Accelerate Commercial Vehicle Electrification 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 1:01PM by PIB Chennai 
 The Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) will host the ‘eCV Dialogue’, a two-day national-level forum on January 21 and 22, 2027, aimed at accelerating electric mobility in India’s medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicle sector. Held under the patronage of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India, the event will convene Union Ministers, policymakers, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), commercial fleet operators, logistics enterprises, and researchers on a single platform to develop actionable policy recommendations, infrastructure Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and national transition roadmaps. 
 Highlighting the need for the initiative, Prof. V. Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras, noted that medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles account for roughly 40 per cent of on-road transport fuel consumption and nearly 25 per cent of India’s oil import bill, while electric trucks currently represent only about 0.2 per cent of commercial vehicle sales. He stated that the dialogue seeks to foster coordinated value-chain action toward India’s Net Zero 2070 goal. 
 Prof. CS Shankar Ram, Associate Dean (ICSR) and Principal Investigator, Centre of Excellence for Zero Emission Trucking (CoEZET), IIT Madras, emphasized that electrifying commercial transport is vital for energy security and sustainable logistics. 
 Departing from conventional speech-based conferences, the eCV Dialogue will adopt a deliberative, workshop-driven format inspired by the ancient Indian tradition of ‘Shastrartha’. According to Prof. Karthick Athmanathan, Professor of Practice, Department of Engineering Design, IIT Madras, closed-door technical and policy sessions will rigorously examine incentives, battery systems, charging infrastructure, safety standards, and financing mechanisms to produce implementable solutions. 
 *** 
 SS/PS

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: PM-WANI Scheme: Expanding Aﬀordable Public Wi-Fi Connectivity and Promoting Digital Inclusion in Haryana
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Communications 
 PM-WANI Scheme: Expanding Aﬀordable Public Wi-Fi Connectivity and Promoting Digital Inclusion in Haryana 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 2:43PM by PIB Chandigarh 
 The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, is promoting the Prime Minister’s Wi-Fi Access Network Interface (PM-WANI) Scheme to expand aﬀordable broadband connectivity through public Wi-Fi hotspots across the country, including Haryana. 
 Designed as a decentralised, entrepreneur-led framework, PM-WANI strengthens India’s digital public infrastructure by enabling local shopkeepers, small businesses, and institutions to set up public Wi-Fi hotspots—bridging last-mile connectivity gaps while creating sustainable supplementary income streams. 
 Haryana’s Progress under PM-WANI 
 Haryana secures the 5th spot nationwide in PM-WANI deployment! With 18,546 Wi-Fi hotspots onboarded as of October 31, 2026 (contributing to India's total of 4,32,906 hotspots), Haryana LSA continues to drive initiatives to expand public Wi-Fi access and boost participation across the State. 
 Key Features of the PM-WANI Scheme. The PM-WANI ecosystem comprises four key components: 
 Public Data Oﬃce (PDO): Public Data Office will establish, maintain, and operate PM-WANI compliant Wi-Fi Hotspots and provide last-mile connectivity to deliver Broadband services to subscribers by procuring internet bandwidth from telecom service providers and/ or internet service providers. Local entrepreneurs and shopkeepers can establish and operate public Wi-Fi hotspots without requiring a separate DoT licence or registration. 
 Public Data Oﬃce Aggregator (PDOA): Public Data Office Aggregator will provide aggregation services such as authorization and accounting to PDOs, thereby facilitating PDOs in providing services to the end consumer. 
 App Provider: App Provider will develop an Application to register users and discover and display PM-WANI compliant Wi-Fi Hotspots in the proximity for accessing the internet service and also authenticate the potential Broadband users. 
 Central Registry: Central Registry will maintain the details of App Providers, PDOAs, and PDOs. It is currently maintained by the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DoT). 
 Benefits and Recent Policy Initiatives 
 The scheme provides citizens with an additional option for accessing aﬀordable 
 broadband connectivity and facilitates online education, e-governance, digital payments and other internet-based services. It also empowers local entrepreneurs to generate supplementary income by establishing public Wi-Fi hotspots. 
 To accelerate adoption, DoT has introduced several reforms, including: 
 Retail FTTH Utilization: Permitting PDOs to use regular Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) broadband connections to set up hotspots. 
 Aﬀordable Tariﬀ Ceiling: Under TRAI’s Tariﬀ Order dated June 16, 2025, Service Providers are mandated to oﬀer retail FTTH broadband plans (up to 200 Mbps) to PDOs at tariﬀs not exceeding twice the corresponding retail consumer tariff. 
 Infrastructure Sharing: Allowing multiple Wi-Fi access points to operate through a single backhaul connection. 
 Plug-and-Play Integration: Facilitating the seamless onboarding of existing home and business Wi-Fi access points into the PM-WANI network. 
 Inter-PDOA Roaming & MDO: Enabling seamless user roaming across diﬀerent PDOAs alongside Mobile Data Oﬄoading (MDO) in association with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). 
 Haryana LSA’s Initiatives 
 Haryana LSA is conducting targeted awareness drives and facilitation workshops across the State to engage local entrepreneurs, shopkeepers, educational institutions, Common Service Centres (CSCs), and market associations. Special emphasis is being placed on rural and semi-urban pockets to ensure equitable broadband access. 
 Haryana LSA invites aspiring entrepreneurs, small businesses, and institutions to leverage these simplified policy provisions, onboard as PDOs, and contribute toward building a digitally empowered Haryana. 
 For scheme guidelines, registered PDOAs, and onboarding procedures, interested stakeholders may visit the official portal: https://pmwani.gov.in/wani 
 Through PM-WANI, the Government of India continues to advance its Digital India vision by democratising public Wi-Fi infrastructure, fostering micro-entrepreneurship, and ensuring inclusive digital connectivity for all.

 The Consumer Education and Protection Cell (CEPC), Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Chandigarh, conducted a week-long cyber fraud awareness campaign across nine educational institutions in Amritsar, Ludhiana and Jalandhar from November 16 to 20, 2026. https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: 11th International Conference TSAB–IRF-2026 concludes at National Library
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
 11th International Conference TSAB–IRF-2026 concludes at National Library 
 ZSI Director Dr. Dhriti Banerjee conferred with Lifetime Achievement Award 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 1:45PM by PIB Kolkata 
 Kolkata November 25, 2026 
 The Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), Kolkata, in joint collaboration with the Agricultural Technology Development Society (ATDS), Ghaziabad, successfully organised the 11th International Conference on “Transforming Science, Agriculture and Biodiversity Conservation: Innovations for a Resilient Future” (TSAB–IRF-2026) at National Library of India, Kolkata, on November 22–23, 2026.
The two-day international conclave brought together leading scientists, academicians, researchers, and students from across India and abroad to exchange scientific insights and deliberate on emerging challenges and innovative solutions in biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture, and environmental resilience.
The conference was graced by Dr. Dhriti Banerjee, Director, ZSI, as the Chief Guest; Prof. Amar P. Garg, Former Vice-Chancellor, SIET, Meerut, as the Distinguished Guest; and Prof. Dilfuza Jabborova as the Special Guest.
Other prominent dignitaries present included Prof. H. Shivananda Murthy, Dr. Jitendra Kumar, Dr. P. R. More (Convenor), Dr. Anant Kumar (President, ATDS), and Dr. T. S. Pathan (Conference Director). The event was coordinated by Dr. Devanshu Gupta, Scientist-D, ZSI, Kolkata, and Dr. Joginder Singh, Secretary, ATDS, who served as the Organising Secretaries.
A major highlight of the event was the conferment of the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award upon Dr. Dhriti Banerjee, Director, ZSI, in recognition of her exemplary leadership and enduring contributions to the field of Zoology. The honour acknowledges her pioneering research in faunal taxonomy and her pivotal role in advancing scientific knowledge and strengthening India’s biodiversity research community.
The dignitaries also released the official conference souvenir, documenting the scientific themes, abstracts, and scholarly contributions of the conclave.
TSAB–IRF-2026 recorded extensive national and international outreach, registering 424 participation entries (139 offline and 285 online) representing 23 Indian States and five foreign nations—Bangladesh, Kenya, Malaysia, Uzbekistan, and Italy.
Featuring 15 keynote addresses by eminent domain experts, the interdisciplinary platform witnessed active scientific contributions from researchers representing premier institutions, including:
Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)
CSIR–National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI)
CSIR–Institute of Minerals and Materials Technology (CSIR-IMMT)
ICAR–Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (ICAR-CIFA)
ICAR–Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI)
Banaras Hindu University (BHU)
TERI School of Advanced Studies
The deliberations at TSAB–IRF-2026 culminated in eight actionable policy and research recommendations aimed at harmonising agricultural productivity with ecological preservation as the following:
Promotion of Morphotaxonomy: Strengthening classical and integrative morphotaxonomy for accurate identification and documentation of diverse life forms.
Biodiversity Protection: Enhancing habitat protection and targeted conservation strategies for native flora and fauna.
Pollinator Conservation: Implementing dedicated measures for the protection and conservation of pollinators critical to ecosystem health and crop yields.
Eco-Friendly Farming: Accelerating the adoption of natural farming, bio-fertilisers, biopesticides, and biochar.
Chemical Reduction: Phasing down synthetic agrochemicals in favour of Integrated Pest Management (IPM).
Sustainable Aquaculture: Promoting ecologically sound and sustainable aquaculture practices.
Water Security: Enforcing mandatory rainwater harvesting systems to bolster groundwater recharge.
Plastic Mitigation: Implementing a phased reduction in the use of polythene and single-use plastics.
Addressing the gathering, speakers underscored that biodiversity conservation forms the bedrock of ecological stability, food security, and sustainable development. Through the successful execution of TSAB–IRF-2026, the ZSI reaffirmed its commitment to fostering interdisciplinary research, taxonomic excellence, and international scientific cooperation to address pressing global environmental challenges.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: MY Bharat Bengaluru Urban Organises Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad on Constitution Day
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports 
 MY Bharat Bengaluru Urban Organises Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad on Constitution Day 
 200 Youth Participants Engage in Dialogue on Viksit Bharat@2047 and the Importance of a Drug-Free India Padmashree Awardee Dr. S. G Susheelamma Sumangali, and Ms. Harshita Tater Share Their Inspiring Journeys with the Amrit Peedhi 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:07PM by PIB Bengaluru 
 Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, successfully organised the Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad Programme at CHRIST (Deemed to be university), Bengaluru urban, on 25th November 2026, on the run up to Constitution Day. With the overarching theme “Viksit Bharat@2047”, the programme brought together young citizens to understand India's developmental journey, engage with the vision of a developed India and recognise their role in nation-building. 
 The programme was part of a nationwide initiative being organised across 500+ law colleges in more than 30 States and Union Territories, covering over 600 districts. Through this extensive institutional outreach, MY Bharat seeks to channelise the potential of the Amrit Peedhi towards nation-building by creating opportunities for young people to participate in meaningful dialogue, exchange ideas and take collective action on issues of national importance. 
 As a key component of the programme, Mr. Varun arya delivered a presentation on the theme “Viksit Bharat@2047”, taking students through India's developmental journey and its vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047. The presentation highlighted the country's progress in poverty reduction and socio economic transformation, the significant strides made in addressing Left-Wing Extremism (Naxalism), and the importance of building a healthy, empowered and addiction-free society. It also emphasised how substance abuse poses a serious challenge to individual potential, family well-being, societal progress and national productivity. The presentation reinforced the message that a Nasha Mukt Bharat is fundamental to realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, with youth playing a decisive role in driving this transformation. 
 The programme also provided students with an opportunity to interact with distinguished personalities, including Dr. S.G Susheelamma, Padma Awardee, and Ms.Harshita Tater, Para-Athlete, who shared their personal journeys, experiences and insights. Through their inspiring accounts of perseverance, determination, discipline and achievement, they encouraged young participants to pursue their aspirations, overcome challenges and contribute meaningfully to society. 
 Marking the significance of Constitution Day, participants collectively undertook a reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India, reaffirming their commitment to the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. The collective reading served as a reminder of the responsibility of every citizen, particularly the youth, in upholding constitutional ideals and contributing towards the vision of a Viksit Bharat. 
 The programme witnessed enthusiastic participation from 200 students and youths, who actively engaged in the presentations, interactions and discussions. Through this initiative, MY Bharat sought to strengthen awareness about substance abuse, promote responsible choices and encourage young people to become ambassadors of a Nasha Mukt Bharat. 
 Through the Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad Programme, MY Bharat continues to provide a platform for Yuva Shakti to engage, lead and contribute to nation-building. By bringing together India's developmental aspirations, inspiring role models and the message of an addiction-free society, the initiative seeks to transform awareness into action and youth participation into a sustained movement for change. 
 The journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047 is a collective endeavour, and its success rests on the choices, commitment and contribution of today's youth. The programme encouraged participants to carry forward the message of “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat” beyond the event and inspire their peers, families and communities to embrace healthy, productive and addiction-free lives. 
 For more information about MY Bharat and opportunities for youth participation, visit http://www.mybharat.gov.in.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas to visit PDEU; to see National Core Repository and interact with students on Energy Transition
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas 
 Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas to visit PDEU; to see National Core Repository and interact with students on Energy Transition 
 Senior officers of ONGC and IOCL to accompany the Hon'ble Minister 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:36PM by PIB Ahmedabad 
 HHon'ble Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, will visit Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), Gandhinagar, on Friday (27th November).. The Hon'ble Minister is scheduled to arrive on campus at 2:30 p.m. and will be accompanied by senior officers of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL). During the visit, the Hon'ble Minister will tour the National Core Repository and will thereafter interact with a select group of PDEU students on the theme of Energy Transition.
 National Core Repository 
 The National Core Repository (NCR) at Gandhinagar was established under the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, as a national facility for the preservation, curation and scientific study of drill cores recovered from India's sedimentary basins. Cores held at national repositories are treated as a national asset, with access governed by DGH, and constitute a primary scientific record of the country's subsurface. The facility supports basin studies, reservoir characterisation and exploration research by academia, national oil companies and industry.
 PDEU will be housing about 1 lakh metre cores from onshore and offshore basins of India. To start with the university is focusing on 5 basins. 
 Interaction with students on Energy Transition 
 The Hon'ble Minister will address and take questions from students drawn from across the University's schools of petroleum technology, energy technology, management and liberal studies. The session is intended as an open exchange on India's energy transition pathway, the role of natural gas as a transition fuel, green hydrogen, biofuels and ethanol blending, carbon capture, and the skills and research capacity the sector will require of the next generation of energy professionals.
 PDEU and the energy transition 
 The University was reconstituted from Pandit Deendayal Petroleum University to Pandit Deendayal Energy University in 2020, reflecting a deliberate widening of its mandate from hydrocarbons to the full energy spectrum. Research at the University today spans solar, wind, hydrogen, geothermal, bioenergy and energy storage, aligned to India's net-zero commitment.
 Among the University's dedicated facilities are the Centre of Excellence for Geothermal Energy (CEGE), established in 2013 with the support of the Government of Gujarat; the Solar Research and Development Centre; the Centre for Biofuel and Bioenergy Studies; the International Automobile Centre of Excellence; and the SIEMENS Centre of Excellence. The Department of Science and Technology sanctioned a Technology Enabling Centre at PDEU in 2023 on the theme of Energy, Health and Water, to carry laboratory research through prototype, validation and field trial to industry adoption.
 In a demonstration that drew national attention, a PDEU team produced and stored green hydrogen at the Geothermal Park at Unai, Navsari, using an Organic Rankine Cycle system that couples geothermal and solar input to deliver round-the-clock generation. The project was recognised among the leading entries in the Industry–Academia Collaboration category at the FICCI Bharat R&D Summit 2024. The University has also been designated by DGH for Enhanced Oil Recovery screening work, alongside ONGC's Institute of Reservoir Studies and the Indian Institutes of Technology.
 The visit follows SEQUENCE 2026 – Summit of the Future, the University's international partnership-building summit held on campus on 24 August 2026, which brought together diplomatic missions, funding agencies and institutions across five frontier domains to build research and industry partnerships. Energy transition was among the domains taken up at the Summit, and several of the collaborations initiated there are now under development.
 About PDEU 
 Pandit Deendayal Energy University was established in 2007 by an Act of the Gujarat State Legislature and is located on the Knowledge Corridor at Raisan, Gandhinagar. The University offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes across engineering, energy technology, management, science and liberal studies, and is accredited with an A++ grade by NAAC.

https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.title: Dr. Neelima Satyam Elected President-Elect of AGU Natural Hazards Section
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx.body:
Ministry of Education 
 Dr. Neelima Satyam Elected President-Elect of AGU Natural Hazards Section 
 A landmark international achievement for Indian science and IIT Indore 
 Posted On: 
 25 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Bhopal 
 In a moment of immense pride for India and its scientific community, Dr. Neelima Satyam Devarakonda, Institute Chair Professor in the Department of Civil Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Indore, has been elected President-Elect of the Natural Hazards Section of the American Geophysical Union (AGU) for the 2027–2028 term. The election results were announced by AGU on November 24, 2026. With this appointment, she will also become a member of the AGU Council. 
 The American Geophysical Union (AGU) is one of the world's leading scientific organisations, bringing together researchers, academicians and professionals working across Earth and space sciences. Its Natural Hazards Section provides an international platform for advancing scientific understanding of natural hazards, including earthquakes, landslides, floods and other geophysical risks, and promoting research that contributes to disaster risk reduction and community resilience. 
 Dr. Neelima Satyam has made significant contributions to research in geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, seismic hazards, landslide risk assessment, debris flow modelling and disaster-resilient infrastructure. Her work focuses on bridging scientific understanding with engineering applications and technological innovations to address real-world challenges associated with natural hazards. 
 Her association with AGU includes serving as a member of the Natural Hazards Executive Committee, Canvassing Committee and Section Awards Committee. Her contributions to the scientific community have been recognised through several prestigious honours. She received the AGU Natural Hazards Mitigation Award in 2025 and was selected as a 2026 AGU Union Fellow. She has also been recognised with the 2026 Devendra Lal Memorial Medal. 
 Dr. Neelima Satyam holds a Ph.D. and M.Tech. from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi and a B.Tech. from Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati. At IIT Indore, she has also served as Head of the Department of Civil Engineering, contributing to academic leadership, research advancement and institutional development. 
 A Historic First for an Indian Woman Scientist 
 Dr. Neelima Satyam's election marks a historic milestone, as she becomes the first woman scientist from India to lead the Natural Hazards Section of the American Geophysical Union. This achievement is particularly significant because she will be assuming this prestigious international leadership position while continuing to serve at an Indian academic institution, IIT Indore. 
 Notably, while earlier leaders of Indian origin who held this position were affiliated with institutions in the United States during their tenure, Dr. Neelima Satyam will be leading the section from India. This distinction underscores the growing global recognition of India's scientific capabilities and the increasing stature of Indian academic institutions in international research and scientific leadership. 
 As President-Elect, Dr. Neelima will contribute to the leadership and strategic direction of the Natural Hazards Section, working alongside leading researchers and experts from across the world. Her role will provide opportunities to strengthen international scientific collaboration and advance research addressing global challenges related to natural hazards, disaster preparedness and community resilience. 
 This prestigious international recognition brings immense pride to IIT Indore, Madhya Pradesh and the entire Indian scientific community. It is also an inspiration to young researchers, particularly women pursuing careers in science, technology and engineering, demonstrating that Indian scientists can achieve leadership positions in some of the world's most respected scientific organisations while contributing from institutions in India. 
 Dr. Neelima Satyam's election is not only a personal academic achievement but also a significant milestone for India's growing presence in global scientific research and leadership.
