https://www.mea.gov.in/press-releases?dt.body:
19 November, 2026 
 PM to inaugurate First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum (November 19, 2026)
 Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum on 20 November 2026 at around 5:30 PM at Purana Qila, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
2. Being held from 20 to 22 November 2026, the Forum aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of the region, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation.
 3. The initiative builds upon the proposal made by the Prime Minister at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China in 2025 to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue under the SCO framework. The proposal was subsequently welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration of SCO. 
 4. The inaugural ceremony will feature “Civilisations in Conversation - Cultural Show”, a presentation combining music, dance, visual storytelling and narration. Based on the theme “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - The World Is One Family”, it will highlight cultural connections across India and Eurasia.
5. The Forum will also feature exhibitions showcasing India's archaeological, artistic and literary heritage titled “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence.” It will offer an immersive account of Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE, including excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. The “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion - Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll” will showcase an illustrated scroll reflecting India's rich epic and artistic traditions.
 6. Four thematic sessions will be held on 21 and 22 November, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives. Discussions will cover cultural expressions such as music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine, traditional games; shared traditions in art and architecture; language and literary traditions, including scripts and manuscripts; and monastic trails and philosophical traditions.

https://www.mea.gov.in/press-releases?dt.body:
17 November, 2026 
 Quad Leaders’ Summit Joint Press Release
 On November 17, 2026, we — President Donald J. Trump of the United States, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese of Australia, Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India, and Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae of Japan — met for a Quad Leaders’ Summit in Manila. This year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Prime Minister Abe Shinzo of Japan in 2016. A decade on, that vision is stronger than ever. Together, we have shown that the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity. We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability. We express grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions. We are securing critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future including investments and deployment of trusted Artificial Intelligence (AI)*, and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance. We commit to work together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific. We are working with regional partners to tackle shared challenges and drive opportunities to deliver tangible benefits to the Indo-Pacific.
 ● We announce the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum which is scheduled to be held in early 2027, bringing together business leaders, government officials, and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater business ties across our private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific. 
 ● We affirm the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta. The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific. 
 ● We are proud to welcome the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration , a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness. In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer. 
 ● We are proud of progress under the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience , which has expanded access to secure and trusted communications infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific. Today, we welcome an expansion of Australia’s contribution to the Partnership to focus on electricity cables, strengthening regional energy security and connectivity. We also welcome upcoming undersea cables projects in the Indian Ocean which are intended to strengthen regional connectivity. 
 ● We acknowledge the rapid increase in the number and scale of cyber incidents in the region and announce enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation , through which we plan to work together to achieve an open and secure cyberspace. 
 ● We unequivocally condemn terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations , including cross-border terrorism, and commit to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism. 
 We reaffirm our unwavering support for ASEAN centrality and unity. Together, we are committed to upholding a free and open Indo-Pacific.
